title: A novel natural ventilation corridor approach for airshed analysis and multiscale intervention hotspot identification via hydrological simulation
summary: Urban areas face increasing environmental challenges that threaten public health. Nature-based Solutions (NbS) provide mitigation, yet their success relies heavily on thoughtful spatial planning that considers the interaction between air an
content: Urban areas face increasing environmental challenges that threaten public health. Nature-based Solutions (NbS) provide mitigation, yet their success relies heavily on thoughtful spatial planning that considers the interaction between air and morphology. This study presents a computationally efficient GIS-based hydrological approach using an airflow-integrated DEM (AF-DEM) to delineate regional airshed impacting urban areas and to identify multiscale Natural Ventilation Corridors (NVCs) as ordered intervention hotspots where airflow converges from larger areas. This approach offers reliable airflow patterns at multiple scales with lower computational demand compared to traditional CFD and WRF models.” The regional airshed for Delhi-NCT was identified at 3000 m resolution through national-scale airflow analysis. and intervention hotspots were then mapped at 300 m (mesoscale) for the regional airshed and 30 m (microscale) for the city boundary. Results show that the regional airshed stretches approximately 198 km east-west and 307 km north-south. Also, it shows that 82% of mesoscale intervention hotspots lie in low-plant zones, which cover only 12% of the area. Microscale intervention hotspots are predominantly in low-plant (45%) and open low-rise (28%) areas, which comprise just 3% and 42% of the city's area, respectively. Prioritizing these intervention hotspots for NbS interventions establishes an efficient, data-driven approach to developing healthier, more resilient cities globally.

title: Phosphorus source shapes rhizosphere microbiome assembly and plant oxidative stress regulation in a volcanic Andisol: a path-analysis approach
summary: Volcanic Andisols in southern Chile severely limit pasture productivity due to their high phosphorus (P) sorption capacity. This study evaluated how contrasting P sources shape the rhizosphere microbiome of perennial ryegrass ( Lolium peren
content: Volcanic Andisols in southern Chile severely limit pasture productivity due to their high phosphorus (P) sorption capacity. This study evaluated how contrasting P sources shape the rhizosphere microbiome of perennial ryegrass ( Lolium perenne ) and the pathways linking microbial community composition, plant biochemical responses, and biomass production under P-limiting conditions. A greenhouse experiment using an Andisol (Freire series) tested four P sources; Triple Superphosphate (TSP), Phosphate Rock (PR), Cattle Dung (CD), and Poultry Manure (PM); at two nitrogen (N) rates (100 and 200 mg kg -1 ) alongside no-P control that received the same two N rates and basal nutrients but no added P. Rhizosphere communities were characterized by 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing coupled with functional gene prediction (PICRUSt2), antioxidant enzyme activity and lipid peroxidation markers (superoxide dismutase, catalase, malondialdehyde), P-starvation transporter and phosphatase gene expression ( LpPHT1;1 , LpPHT1;4 , LpPAP1 ), and soil chemistry. P source was the dominant driver of both plant performance and community composition, with N rate exerting a secondary, modulatory role; attenuating P-starvation gene expression at higher doses and subtly influencing community beta-diversity. Soil P availability, pH, and exchangeable aluminum were the significant drivers of community structure. Path analysis revealed that the rhizosphere microbiome had no significant direct effect on shoot P uptake but was strongly associated with reduced foliar oxidative stress (β = -0.759, p < 0.001), with its indirect effect on shoot biomass statistically consistent with mediation through this antioxidant buffering response. Organic amendments enriched predicted genes related to P mineralization and biological N-P cycling while suppressing denitrification-associated genes. These findings suggest that in high P-fixing volcanic soils, rhizosphere community shifts benefit plant growth primarily by alleviating P deficiency-induced oxidative stress rather than by directly enhancing P uptake, highlighting the agronomic value of organic amendments beyond nutrient supply alone.

title: Prioritizing hydrogen deployment across hard-to-electrify sectors based on system-level environmental performance
summary: Hydrogen is widely considered as a key option for decarbonizing hard-to-electrify sectors; however, identifying where and how it should be deployed requires system-level, multi-impact assessment to avoid environmental burden shifting. This
content: Hydrogen is widely considered as a key option for decarbonizing hard-to-electrify sectors; however, identifying where and how it should be deployed requires system-level, multi-impact assessment to avoid environmental burden shifting. This study aims to determine environmentally optimal hydrogen deployment pathways and sectoral priorities for Finland’s energy transition using a scenario-based, system-level LCA. The analysis integrates multiple hydrogen production pathways and their conversion into hydrogen-derived fuels and chemicals, which are deployed across steel, shipping, aviation, heavy-duty transport, chemical production, and oil refining sectors under alternative transition scenarios. Environmental performance is evaluated across five midpoint impact categories: climate change, acidification, fine particulate matter formation, marine eutrophication, and ozone depletion, calculated by using the ReCiPe method. Results show that 100 % wind-powered electrolysis-based hydrogen delivers the highest overall environmental performance, reducing national climate change impacts by 80 % (from 30.8 to 6.2 Mt CO 2 ,eq./a) and decreasing other environmental impacts by 47–76 %. Beyond conventional LCA results, this study introduces two novel deployment priority indices (DPIs) to translate multi-impact outcomes into decision-relevant guidance. The system-weighted DPI identifies sectors where hydrogen deployment yields the greatest reduction in national environmental impacts, while the sector-intrinsic DPI ranks transitions based on their internal multi-impact environmental efficiency, independent of sector size. By jointly applying these two DPIs within a unified system-level LCA framework, this study provides a novel, transparent basis for prioritizing hydrogen deployment across sectors, enabling strategic, impact-driven decision-making and efficient allocation of renewable energy resources.

title: Journal of Green Economy and Optimization Research (JGEOR), Volume 1, Issue 2 (2026)
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: The second issue of the Journal of Green Economy and Optimization Research (JGEOR) presents interdisciplinary scholarly contributions addressing contemporary challenges in green economy, sustainable development, environmental economics, gre
content: The second issue of the Journal of Green Economy and Optimization Research (JGEOR) presents interdisciplinary scholarly contributions addressing contemporary challenges in green economy, sustainable development, environmental economics, green finance, digital transformation, optimization, environmental management and related fields. This issue continues the journal’s commitment to advancing high-quality, evidence-based and policy-relevant research with academic and practical significance.

title: Evaluating green strategies in ports using a decision support framework and integrating stakeholder perspectives: a case study of the Persian Gulf
summary: Ports are increasingly vital in the international transport system, commerce, and economic growth. Growing awareness and rising expectations for sustainability require ports to address environmental concerns and meet regulatory standards. T
content: Ports are increasingly vital in the international transport system, commerce, and economic growth. Growing awareness and rising expectations for sustainability require ports to address environmental concerns and meet regulatory standards. This study examines the prioritisation of green strategies in ports by capturing and pooling the perspectives of port management bodies (PMBs) and port stakeholder groups (PSGs). In this study, a multi-criteria decision-making framework, namely Fuzzy ZE, is applied to the green strategy groups identified through a comprehensive narrative extraction. Insights to parametrise the model are derived from selected stakeholders in ports in the Persian Gulf region. The study identifies Policy Frameworks and Instruments, Energy Efficiency, and Renewable Energy Production as the top strategies; this highlights the importance of regulations, energy optimisation, and clean energy transitions. The assessment of the stakeholder groups also highlights the need to engage influential groups such as regulators and terminal operators, local communities, and employees to support long-term strategic goals. The findings provide a framework for aligning green strategies with stakeholder priorities and offer insights for policymakers to enhance sustainability and competitiveness within the port sector. Insights from this study can also inform global best practices to advance sustainable port management.

title: Exergy and environmental sustainability assessment of PV integrated greenhouse cucumber production
summary: Abstract This study examines the thermodynamic and environmental performance of cucumber produced under greenhouse conditions in Türkiye with a holistic approach. The analysis, conducted in the provinces of Kırklareli and Konya, calculated
content: Abstract This study examines the thermodynamic and environmental performance of cucumber produced under greenhouse conditions in Türkiye with a holistic approach. The analysis, conducted in the provinces of Kırklareli and Konya, calculated cumulative energy consumption (CEnC), cumulative exergy consumption (CExC), and cumulative CO 2 emissions (CCO 2 E), with a functional unit of one ton of product. In addition, two important sustainability indicators, namely Cumulative Degree of Perfection (CDP) and Renewability Indicator (RI), were calculated based on exergy calculations. According to the results, CEnC was 260.16 MJ/ton, CExC was 1459.82 MJ/ton, and CCO 2 E was 31.13 kg/ton in Kırklareli, while these values were determined to be 324.38 MJ/ton, 2521.12 MJ/ton, and 50.91 kg/ton, respectively, in Konya. This difference indicates that irrigation and electricity use increase the energy and exergy intensity in Konya. Exergy based sustainability indicators, CDP and RI values, were calculated as 0.73 and − 0.36 for Kırklareli, and 0.42 and − 1.36 for Konya, respectively. These values reveal the high dependence of current production processes on non-renewable energy sources. When photovoltaic (PV) panels were used to supply electricity, the CDP in Kırklareli increased from 0.73 to 0.77, and the RI improved from − 0.36 to -0.30. In Konya, the CDP value rose to 0.51, and the RI to -0.96. These results suggest that PV integration has the potential to improve renewability indicators, especially in energy intensive regions. The findings indicate that, within the scope of this analysis, the sustainability of greenhouse cucumber production could be enhanced through optimized resource management and PV systems.

title: India's Road to A $5 Trillion Economy: Opportunities and Challenges
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: India is on an ambitious journey to achieve a $5 trillion economy, driven by rapid digital transformation, infrastructure development, and industrial growth. This article explores the key drivers, opportunities, and challenges in India's ec
content: India is on an ambitious journey to achieve a $5 trillion economy, driven by rapid digital transformation, infrastructure development, and industrial growth. This article explores the key drivers, opportunities, and challenges in India's economic trajectory. Major opportunities include technological advancements, manufacturing expansion under ‘Make in India,’ rising consumer demand, and renewable energy investments. However, India faces significant challenges such as unemployment, income inequality, inflation, fiscal deficit, global economic uncertainties, and climate change. Addressing these hurdles through policy reforms, investment in human capital, and sustainable development strategies will be crucial for achieving long-term economic stability and growth. The study highlights the need for inclusive economic policies to ensure that growth benefits all sections of society. With strong policy interventions, investmentfriendly initiatives, and global partnerships, India can successfully navigate its challenges and emerge as a global economic powerhouse.

title: A visible light perfect absorber based on titanium nitride (TiN)
summary: To alleviate the global contradiction between energy supply and demand and develop renewable energy systems at the same time, this paper proposes a perfect absorber which based on TiN andr consists of a TiN ring array layer, a SiO₂ insulati
content: To alleviate the global contradiction between energy supply and demand and develop renewable energy systems at the same time, this paper proposes a perfect absorber which based on TiN andr consists of a TiN ring array layer, a SiO₂ insulating layer, and a TiN reflective layer from top to bottom. It achieves an average absorptivity as high as 89.741% across the 300-1000 nm visible to near-infrared wavelength range. The absorber features a relatively simple structure and great geometric tolerance, reducing fabrication complexity and cost. Relying on the high melting point, thermal resistance, and insulation of TiN and SiO₂, it establishes an efficient synergistic mechanism of "incidence-transmission-absorption", ultimately realizing near-perfect absorption across the entire spectrum and promoting the practical and large-scale development of thermal energy utilization technologies.

title: Pro-ecological microwave-assisted extraction of phytochemicals from Moringa oleifera Lam. leaves: Multi-response surface optimization and predictive modeling
summary: This study presents a pro-ecological approach for the efficient recovery of natural antioxidants from plant matrixes by optimizing the green microwave-assisted extraction (MAE) of bioactive compounds from Moringa oleifera Lam.leaves.A centr
content: This study presents a pro-ecological approach for the efficient recovery of natural antioxidants from plant matrixes by optimizing the green microwave-assisted extraction (MAE) of bioactive compounds from Moringa oleifera Lam.leaves.A central composite design (CCD) coupled with response surface methodology (RSM) was employed to model and evaluate extraction performance as a function of eco-friendly process parameters: ethanol concentration (X 1 , % v/v), liquid-to-solid ratio (X 2 , mL g -1 ), and extraction time (X 3 , s).The predictive response models effectively mapped three independent targets: total phenolic content (TPC, Y 1 ), total flavonoid content (TFC, Y 2 ), and reducing sugar content (RSC, Y 3 ).The individual optimal conditions (X 1 , X 2 , X 3 ) to maximize yields were successfully determined to be (40% v/v, 50:1 mL g -1 , 85 s) for TPC, (60% v/v, 50:1 mL g -1 , 90 s) for TFC, and (20% v/v, 45:1 mL g -1 , 100 s) for RSC.Under these respective parameters, experimental maximums reached 23.5 mg GAE/g, 20.8 mg RE/g, and 76.3 mg GE/g, closely validating the predictive simulations.Strong positive correlations were observed between antioxidant activity (AA) and both TPC (R 2 = 0.78) and TFC (R 2 = 0.73).These findings demonstrate that optimized MAE serves as an energy-saving and sustainable bioprocess for isolating high-value phytochemicals with minimal environmental impact.

title: Video Abstract: Electro-Driven Membrane Separations for Sustainable Bio-Based Chemical Recovery
summary: This research addresses one of the most critical bottlenecks in circular biotechnology: the high energy and economic costs of downstream purification in biorefineries. While microbial synthesis of renewable chemicals has advanced rapidly, t
content: This research addresses one of the most critical bottlenecks in circular biotechnology: the high energy and economic costs of downstream purification in biorefineries. While microbial synthesis of renewable chemicals has advanced rapidly, traditional thermal and chemical recovery methods—such as distillation, evaporation, and precipitation—often account for 50–80% of total processing costs due to the high latent heat of water.This work explores the paradigm shift toward electro-driven membrane systems (EDMS)—including electrodialysis, bipolar membrane configurations, capacitive deionization, and bioelectrochemical systems. Rather than acting as passive filters, these systems serve as active, programmable electrochemical interfaces. By leveraging electric potential gradients alongside localized pH control, EDMS enables precise, speciation-controlled extraction of high-value bioproducts—such as weak organic acids, volatile fatty acids, amino acids, and biogenic nutrients—directly from complex fermentation broths and industrial wastewaters.Key Focus Areas and Scientific Insights:Reactive-Transport Physics: Delves into how field-induced speciation, Donnan exclusion, and electrostatic gating govern selective molecular migration over simple size-exclusion.Energy and Selectivity Tradeoffs: Benchmarks the inescapable thermodynamic nexus between molecular discrimination, volumetric productivity, and specific energy consumption (kWh/kgproduct).Next-Generation Nanomaterials: Evaluates the integration of active 2D nanoconfined laminates (e.g., MXenes, graphene oxide) and metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) engineered for sub-nanometer sieving and electro-catalytic reactivity.Industrial Scale-Up Defenses: Critically analyzes multi-scale performance degradation modes—including electro-biological fouling, mineral scaling, and anodic oxidation—offering actionable mitigation strategies for real-world operations.Decarbonization and Grid Integration: Highlights the integration of continuous in situ product recovery and autonomous control with renewable energy grids, paving the way for low-carbon, circular biorefineries.By linking nanoscale molecular transport with macro-scale techno-economic analysis and life cycle assessment, this research provides a comprehensive blueprint for transforming downstream bioprocesses from energy-intensive purification steps into efficient, sustainable resource recovery engines.

title: Design of visible light absorber based on TiN metamaterials
summary: To address the global energy crisis and advance the development of renewable energy, this paper proposes a metamaterial-based visible light absorber, which consists of a TiN reflective layer, a SiO₂ insulating layer, and a patterned TiN rin
content: To address the global energy crisis and advance the development of renewable energy, this paper proposes a metamaterial-based visible light absorber, which consists of a TiN reflective layer, a SiO₂ insulating layer, and a patterned TiN ring array layer with a combined circular and rectangular geometry. Numerical simulation via COMSOL software demonstrates that the absorber achieves an average absorptivity of 92.6% in the 300–1400 nm wavelength band, with a peak absorptivity of 96.9%. Through investigation of material parameters and electromagnetic field analysis, the proposed structure features the merits of relatively simple configuration and excellent geometric tolerance, which reduces fabrication complexity and cost. The absorber can be directly applied to devices such as solar collectors and thermophotovoltaic systems to improve their energy conversion efficiency, and promote the practical and large-scale development of solar thermal utilization technology. Future work will further optimize the structural parameters of the absorber and explore its application potential in more fields including photothermal power generation and solar seawater desalination.

title: Fintech Market Engagement in Financing Net-Zero Transitions: The Mediating Role of Digital Inclusion
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: This chapter discusses how capital markets (CMs) can be used to distribute the required financial resources to achieve the goals of net-zero emissions and digital inclusion (DI) in the Republic of Africa. It evaluates the ability of such ma
content: This chapter discusses how capital markets (CMs) can be used to distribute the required financial resources to achieve the goals of net-zero emissions and digital inclusion (DI) in the Republic of Africa. It evaluates the ability of such markets to activate the kind of investment that both facilitates the shift in the environment towards sustainability and increases access to digital finance (DF), thus contributing to community growth. It, in particular, explores the primary mechanisms through which the existence of efficient CMs can be utilised to support the green finance (GF) programmes and provide crucial digital infrastructure, among other important ingredients of the sustainable development pathway of Africa. This will involve a discussion of how well green bonds and other international financial instruments will bring capital to renewable energy projects and an assessment of the role played by financial technologies.

title: Broad Fiscal Burden in Asian Energy-Transition Contexts: How Development Levels Condition Growth
summary: Asian economies face the challenge of reducing emissions while sustaining economic growth, yet thegrowth implications of environmental taxation remain uncertain. This study examines whetherbroad tax burden and energy-system conditions are a
content: Asian economies face the challenge of reducing emissions while sustaining economic growth, yet thegrowth implications of environmental taxation remain uncertain. This study examines whetherbroad tax burden and energy-system conditions are associated with economic growth in Asia,whether the tax-growth relationship varies by development level, and whether renewable-energycontext is more closely related to growth or environmental performance. Using an unbalancedcountry-year panel of 20 Asian economies from 1972 to 2024, the analysis applies fixed-effectsregressions with country and year effects and country-clustered standard errors. Because directenergy-tax measures are unavailable, tax revenue as a share of gross domestic product (GDP) isused as a broad fiscal proxy. The baseline model shows no statistically significant relationshipbetween tax revenue and real gross domestic product per capita growth, while the estimatedcoefficient is small and negative. Income-group models suggest heterogeneity around this weakaverage association: the tax-growth relationship is negative for lower-middle-income economiesbut positive for upper-middle-income and high-income economies. Renewable-energy share doesnot significantly moderate the tax-growth relationship, but it is strongly associated with lowercarbon intensity of output. These findings indicate that taxation’s growth associations depend ondevelopment level and not uniform across Asia, while environmental performance is more clearlylinked to energy-system structure than to tax revenue alone. Policy should therefore avoid stand-alone tax instruments, pair fiscal reform with revenue recycling and household protection, andexpand renewable-energy infrastructure.

title: Stochastic energy management strategy for microgrid-connected electric vehicle charging infrastructure
summary: Ensuring the reliability and stability of standalone microgrids (MGs) is fundamental to the effective integration of renewable energy sources, which are inherently uncertain. This work presents a stochastic optimization model using mixed-in
content: Ensuring the reliability and stability of standalone microgrids (MGs) is fundamental to the effective integration of renewable energy sources, which are inherently uncertain. This work presents a stochastic optimization model using mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) to determine the optimal operation of electric vehicle charging stations (EVCS) with transactive control, emphasizing the balance between economic efficiency and system reliability. As a result, deploying EVCS will become a vital strategy for integrating renewable energy. An innovative method for supplying electric power from EV fleets involves using transportation networks as additional infrastructure. This article proposes that transportation networks, EVCS, and MGs can be optimally scheduled under uncertain photovoltaic (PV) generation using transactive control. The stochastic optimization problem is formulated as a mixed-integer nonlinear program and implemented in a moving-horizon framework for real-time onboard operation. The framework is tested on the IEEE 30-bus transmission network. The results show the efficiency of the proposed framework as an improvement tool for economic performance and operational stability in renewable-integrated power markets, and it reduces peak loads through the coordinated charging and discharging of vehicles.

title: Development of straightforward correlations to estimate hydrogen production costs based on wind and PV capacity factors
summary: This work develops straightforward correlations between renewable energy capacity factors and the levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH) across Europe. A detailed simulation model and genetic algorithm optimization were applied to 65 European si
content: This work develops straightforward correlations between renewable energy capacity factors and the levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH) across Europe. A detailed simulation model and genetic algorithm optimization were applied to 65 European sites, considering solar PV (9–20 % capacity factor) and onshore wind (15–50 %). Two scenarios were analyzed: flexible hydrogen production following renewable supply and constant hydrogen supply requiring storage. Results show that LCOH depends strongly on capacity factors, with hybrid wind-solar systems yielding the lowest costs due to higher combined utilization. Under optimal conditions, standalone PV and wind achieve LCOHs of 7.2 €/kg and 5.2 €/kg, respectively, while hybrid systems reach 5.1 €/kg. Constant demand significantly increases costs, especially for PV-only systems, due to storage requirements. The established correlations provide a rapid tool for determining LCOH based on regional renewable potential, facilitating early-stage techno-economic assessments of water electrolysis systems in the European energy landscape.

title: Hydroponic Lettuce and Spinach Production Under Controlled Environments in Urban Pakistan: Growth, Nutritional Quality, and Water-Use Efficiency of NFT and DWC Systems
source: Trends in Animal and Plant Sciences
summary: Rapid urbanization and intensifying water scarcity are placing conventional food-production systems in Pakistan under acute strain, creating an urgent need for resource-efficient alternatives suited to cities.This study evaluated the growth
content: Rapid urbanization and intensifying water scarcity are placing conventional food-production systems in Pakistan under acute strain, creating an urgent need for resource-efficient alternatives suited to cities.This study evaluated the growth, marketable yield, nutritional quality and water-use efficiency of loose-leaf lettuce (Lactuca sativa L. 'Grand Rapids') and flat-leaf spinach (Spinacia oleracea L. 'Viroflay') grown in two soilless systems, the Nutrient Film Technique (NFT) and Deep Water Culture (DWC), against a conventional soil-based control.Hydroponic treatments were applied at three nutrient-solution electrical conductivities (EC1 = 1.5, EC2 = 2.5 and EC3 = 3.5 mS cm⁻¹) in a controlled-environment facility in Rawalpindi, Pakistan, using a completely randomized design with a factorial arrangement, from March to June 2024.NFT at EC3 produced the highest marketable yields (lettuce 4.2 kg m⁻² and spinach 3.7 kg m⁻²), representing increases of 133% and 147% over the soil control, respectively.Nitrate concentrations in all hydroponic produce remained well within international food-safety limits, while vitamin C, leaf chlorophyll (SPAD), total soluble solids and crude protein were significantly higher than in soil-grown plants.Water use in the NFT system was about 90% lower than in conventional cultivation (18.4 versus 186.3 L kg⁻¹ fresh weight).Although hydroponic production costs were higher, retail price premiums for pesticide-free produce yielded favourable economic margins.The results provide baseline, locally grounded evidence supporting the introduction of controlled-environment hydroponics into urban food systems in Pakistan.

title: The causal effect of drought on energy poverty
summary: <title>Abstract</title> We use nationally representative panel data from rural areas and small towns in Ethiopia, matched with fine-resolution weather data, to investigate the impact of drought on energy poverty. Energy poverty is measured
content: <title>Abstract</title> We use nationally representative panel data from rural areas and small towns in Ethiopia, matched with fine-resolution weather data, to investigate the impact of drought on energy poverty. Energy poverty is measured using the Multidimensional Energy Poverty Index (MEPI) and a multidimensional poverty status indicator. Fixed-effects regression estimates show that experiencing drought in the previous production year increases a household’s MEPI score by 0.019 points and raises the probability of being multidimensionally energy poor by 3.8%. We further demonstrate that the primary pathway through which drought affects energy poverty is through its adverse effect on per-capita income: experiencing drought in the previous production period reduces per-capita income by 33.7%. In contrast, we find that the energy poverty of households participating in Ethiopia’s major safety-net intervention—the Productive Safety Net Program (PSNP)—is not significantly affected by drought, suggesting that the program effectively buffers participants from these shocks. Overall, our findings contribute to the growing literature on the economic costs of drought and underscore the critical role of well-targeted safety-net programs in mitigating climate-related vulnerabilities. JEL: Q40; Q54; O13; I32

title: Evaluation of Landfill Gas Generation for Renewable Energy Utilization at Puuwatu Landfill, Kendari City, Indonesia
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: [Objective] Municipal solid waste management in Indonesia faces persistent structural challenges, including inadequate infrastructure, limited implementation of the 3R principle, and continued reliance on landfilling. These conditions are e
content: [Objective] Municipal solid waste management in Indonesia faces persistent structural challenges, including inadequate infrastructure, limited implementation of the 3R principle, and continued reliance on landfilling. These conditions are evident at the Puuwatu landfill in Kendari City, where the high organic waste fraction creates substantial potential for methane generation and greenhouse gas emissions. This study evaluates future methane emissions and assesses their potential for renewable energy recovery to support sustainable urban waste management. [Methodology] Methane generation and landfill gas production were estimated using LandGEM 3.1 for the period 2002–2050 based on historical disposal records and projected municipal solid waste generation. The analysis also quantified methane emissions, electricity generation potential, household energy supply capacity, and the economic value of methane recovery through biogas conversion equivalent to LPG. [Results] Waste generation is projected to increase from 70,140 Mg in 2002 to 274,785 Mg in 2050, while landfill disposal will rise from 51,595 Mg to 202,132 Mg year⁻¹. The high biodegradable fraction (86%) drives LFG production from 1,793 Mg year⁻¹ in 2003 to 66,825 Mg year⁻¹ in 2051. Methane emissions are projected to increase from 479 to 17,847 Mg year⁻¹. Net electricity generation could reach approximately 55 million kWh by 2051, supplying about 9,677 households annually. Methane recovery could also generate approximately IDR 46.76 billion (USD 2.87 million). [Conclusions] Landfill methane represents a valuable renewable energy resource. Its recovery can support urban energy diversification and climate mitigation. These findings highlight the need for technological innovation and supportive policies, particularly for medium-sized cities.

title: Effects of Natural Ventilation On Users’ Comfort in Administrative Buildings in Southwestern Nigerian Federal Polytechnics
summary: This study assessed the effects of natural ventilation on users’ comfort in selected administrative buildings of Federal Polytechnics in Southwestern Nigeria. A mixed-method research design was adopted across Federal Polytechnic Ede, Federa
content: This study assessed the effects of natural ventilation on users’ comfort in selected administrative buildings of Federal Polytechnics in Southwestern Nigeria. A mixed-method research design was adopted across Federal Polytechnic Ede, Federal Polytechnic Ado-Ekiti and Federal Polytechnic Ilaro. Data were obtained through structured questionnaires, physical observation, field measurements and interviews. A total of 295 valid questionnaire responses were analysed alongside qualitative observations. Findings showed that the surveyed buildings were predominantly low- to medium-rise, with cellular office layouts, operable windows and mixed-mode ventilation systems. Natural ventilation was strongly recognised as beneficial, with the statement that natural ventilation improves indoor comfort recording the highest mean score of 3.71, while comfort without mechanical cooling recorded the lowest score of 2.99. Cross ventilation was mostly rated fair, with 40.0% of respondents reporting fair performance, 20.0% poor and 10.2% unavailable. Interview findings further identified thermal discomfort during hot periods, dependence on mechanical cooling and uneven airflow distribution as major concerns. A very strong positive association was observed between ventilation quality and users’ comfort and work performance (r = 0.98), although the relationship was derived from four paired mean observations and should therefore be interpreted cautiously. The study concludes that natural ventilation contributes meaningfully to comfort and workplace performance, but current building configurations do not consistently provide satisfactory conditions. It recommends improved orientation, operable window design, cross-ventilation, shading, airflow pathways and reduced dependence on mechanical cooling in future administrative buildings.

title: Traditional clay-based groundwater recharge systems for sustainable water management and the One Health concept: The Adrar model in Algeria
summary: The purpose of this review is to evaluate the potential of traditional clay-based groundwater recharge systems for improving groundwater sustainability in arid and semi-arid regions, with particular emphasis on the Adrar region of southern
content: The purpose of this review is to evaluate the potential of traditional clay-based groundwater recharge systems for improving groundwater sustainability in arid and semi-arid regions, with particular emphasis on the Adrar region of southern Algeria, while considering their contribution to sustainable water management and the One Health framework.The review also aims to identify the hydrogeological conditions, operational requirements, advantages, and limitations that determine the long-term performance of clay-lined recharge basins.The study adopts a comprehensive literature review and comparative analytical approach by synthesizing recent findings on groundwater depletion, managed aquifer recharge (MAR), hydrogeology, irrigation practices, and traditional clay-based recharge systems.Published hydrogeological data for the Adrar region, including groundwater chemistry, local geological conditions, and engineering characteristics of clay materials, are integrated with evidence from international studies to assess the applicability of this traditional technology under arid climatic conditions.The reviewed evidence indicates that clay-lined recharge basins can effectively increase groundwater recharge efficiency by extending water residence time, reducing evaporation losses, and promoting gradual infiltration where suitable hydrogeological conditions exist.The analysis further shows that the effectiveness of these systems depends on local soil properties, groundwater depth, sediment accumulation, maintenance practices, and irrigation management.Comparative evaluation with other MAR techniques suggests that claybased recharge basins offer important advantages, including low construction cost, operational simplicity, and suitability for water-scarce regions, although their performance remains site-specific and requires continuous monitoring.The review is limited by the availability of published studies and the absence of long-term field validation under different hydrogeological settings.Future investigations should include quantitative monitoring, numerical modeling, and performance assessment under varying climatic conditions.The practical value of this review lies in providing guidance for selecting, designing, and maintaining clay-based recharge systems as low-cost groundwater management solutions.The originality of the study is the integration of hydrogeological, engineering, environmental, and One Health perspectives into a unified assessment of traditional clay-based groundwater recharge technology applicable to arid environments.

title: A deep surrogate modeling approach for distributed control of aggregated air-conditioning loads
summary: Abstract With the increasing penetration of intermittent renewable energy sources, harnessing the flexibility of aggregated air conditioning (AC) loads has become critical for maintaining grid stability. However, existing control strategies
content: Abstract With the increasing penetration of intermittent renewable energy sources, harnessing the flexibility of aggregated air conditioning (AC) loads has become critical for maintaining grid stability. However, existing control strategies often face a trade-off between protecting user privacy and providing a standardized, model-free interface for grid dispatch. This paper proposes a deep surrogate modeling approach that addresses this challenge. We introduce a three-layer “Aggregator-Edge-End user” architecture leveraging a data-driven workflow. At the core of this framework is a hybrid deep learning model combining a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) and a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) network. This model integrates grid regulation signals and a user-willingness factor, enabling it to generate a reliable power-response mapping without requiring sensitive physical parameters. For real-time power allocation, we propose an Improved Distributed Particle Swarm Optimization (IDPSO) algorithm that embeds a LightGBM model to predict thermal dynamics, thereby reducing reliance on traditional thermodynamic models. Large-scale simulations demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves a low power tracking (mean relative error < 0.2%) and robustness to user disturbances. By effectively decoupling control from physical models, this work presents a scalable and market-compatible framework for demand response that reduces direct exposure of user-level data through edge-side aggregation.

title: The Extent of Climate Change Mitigation and Adaptation Strategies Implementation
source: African Journal of Environmental Sciences and Renewable Energy
summary: Climate change and its impacts have escalated in recent decades, and its effects have been felt throughout the globe, making it a global concern and a major issue of the 2030 Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 13 (climate action), which cal
content: Climate change and its impacts have escalated in recent decades, and its effects have been felt throughout the globe, making it a global concern and a major issue of the 2030 Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 13 (climate action), which calls for urgent action to combat climate change and its impacts. In response to this, many nations have developed policies to implement climate strategies through Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), National Adaptation Plans (NAPs), and other specific multi-sectoral climate policies. Despite this, the extent to which these strategies are implemented and their transformative effect has been underexplored. A systematic literature review was conducted to address the research question using the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) from academic databases such as Scopus, Web of Science and Google Scholar and a thematic synthesis revealed patterns in the literature. Implementation of climate strategies remains uneven, fragmented, pilot-scale and predominantly reactive rather than transformative, despite increased adoption of climate policies and planning frameworks; only about 40% of countries that have adopted NAPs systematically assess their implementation, making it difficult to understand their impact. In Africa, strategies such as climate-smart agriculture (CSA), agroforestry, renewable energy and early warning systems are advancing in implementation, although progress is slow, limited in scope and distributed and heavily dependent on donors. In Zambia, despite strong national policy frameworks and donor support, implementation remains limited due to factors such as weak policy-practice linkages, insufficient institutional coordination and socio-economic challenges. Addressing this global implementation gap is important in governance and systems integration, which requires deliberate vulnerability-informed scaling up of strategies that prioritize transformation and sustainability over short-term solutions that continue to make communities poor.

title: Ecological and agronomic impact of internet of things-based drip fertigation powered by solar energy on pakcoy (Brassica rapa L.) and weed dynamics
summary: Conventional irrigation and fertilization methods often lead to resource inefficiency and uncontrolled weed proliferation, which negatively impacts crop productivity and ecological balance.This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a
content: Conventional irrigation and fertilization methods often lead to resource inefficiency and uncontrolled weed proliferation, which negatively impacts crop productivity and ecological balance.This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a smart drip fertigation system integrated with Internet of Things (IoT) and powered by photovoltaic (PV) solar energy in managing water-fertilizer delivery and its subsequent impact on pakcoy (Brassica rapa L.) growth and weed vegetation.The research utilized an experimental design comparing the PV-IoT-based drip system with conventional surface irrigation.Parameters measured included soil moisture stability, water use efficiency, crop yield quality, and weed analysis (species diversity and density).The results indicated that the IoTcontrolled system maintained optimal soil moisture levels, leading to a significant increase in pakcoy growth parameters and most yield quality indicators (plant height, leaf number, fresh and dry weight, and ash content), while vitamin C content remained statistically stable, compared to conventional methods.Notably, the localized water distribution of the drip system substantially suppressed weed growth.The weed analysis revealed a significant reduction in weed density and a shift in species composition, where the smart system prevented the dominance of competitive water-demanding weed species such as T-Grass and Kremah, commonly found in conventional irrigation.The PV-integrated system was designed to operate entirely on solar power without grid dependency, supporting its potential as a sustainable solution for precision agriculture.This study concludes that the integration of PV-IoT in drip fertigation not only optimizes resource conservation but also serves as an effective ecological tool for weed management in vegetable cultivation.

title: Competency-Based Instructional Approach and Students' Academic Performance in Physics in Senior Secondary School in Mkpat Enin Local Government Area
source: International Journal of Social Science Humanity & Management Research
summary: This study investigated the effect of the competency-based instructional approach on students' academic performance in Physics among Senior Secondary School students in Mkpat Enin Local Government Area, Akwa Ibom State. Specifically, the st
content: This study investigated the effect of the competency-based instructional approach on students' academic performance in Physics among Senior Secondary School students in Mkpat Enin Local Government Area, Akwa Ibom State. Specifically, the study determined the difference in the academic performance of students taught electricity using competency-based and expository instructional approaches and examined the influence of gender on students' academic performance under the two instructional approaches. Two research questions and two null hypotheses guided the study. The study adopted a quasi-experimental pretest–posttest non-equivalent group design. The population comprised 1,871 Senior Secondary School Two (SS2) students in sixteen public secondary schools in Mkpat Enin Local Government Area. A sample of 83 students was selected using simple random sampling, comprising 38 students in the competency-based instructional group and 45 students in the expository instructional group. The instrument used for data collection was the Physics Performance Test (PPT), a 20-item multiple-choice achievement test with a reliability coefficient of 0.77 established using the Kuder–Richardson Formula 20 (KR-20). Data collected were analysed using mean and standard deviation to answer the research questions, while Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA) was used to test the hypotheses at the 0.05 level of significance. The findings revealed that students taught electricity using the competency-based instructional approach achieved higher academic performance than those taught using the expository instructional approach. The study also found a significant difference in students' academic performance in favour of the competency-based instructional approach. However, no significant difference was found in the academic performance of male and female students exposed to the two instructional approaches. The study concluded that the competency-based instructional approach is more effective and gender-inclusive than the expository instructional approach for improving students' academic performance in Physics. It was therefore recommended that Physics teachers should adopt the competency-based instructional approach in teaching Physics concepts in secondary schools.

title: CONCEPTUAL FOUNDATIONS OF SOCIAL INNOVATION MANAGEMENT IN MISSION-ORIENTED STATE POLICY
source: State and regions Series Economics and Business
summary: The article provides a theoretical and methodological substantiation of the concept of Social Innovation Management (SIM) as a coordination mechanism within the system of state Mission-Oriented Innovation Policy (MOIPs) in Ukraine. The nece
content: The article provides a theoretical and methodological substantiation of the concept of Social Innovation Management (SIM) as a coordination mechanism within the system of state Mission-Oriented Innovation Policy (MOIPs) in Ukraine. The necessity of transitioning to targeted financing of socially significant strategic goals is substantiated. The evolution of the mission-oriented innovation concept is traced as a means to synchronize efforts aimed at innovative development, enabling the direction of private capital toward achieving national strategic goals. Grounded in Mariana Mazzucato’s "Entrepreneurial State" concept, Smart Specialization (S3), and Open Innovation 2.0, Social Innovation Management is defined as a holistic paradigm that ensures the alignment of national missions with societal needs, guaranteeing social cohesion, resource allocation legitimacy, and institutional sustainability of innovative development. It is demonstrated that SIM integrates technological developments with societal needs, generates trust, reduces transaction costs, and grants public legitimacy to large-scale innovative transformations. Five key missions within the Horizon Europe program (2021–2027) to be implemented by 2030 are presented. The role of social capital as an institutional infrastructure that catalyzes interaction among actors within the Quadruple Helix model (state, business, academia, and civil society) is revealed. In the context of the Law of Ukraine No. 3534-IX, the reform of the scientific and innovation priority system and the transition to foresight studies are analyzed. A triad of strategic national missions is proposed: the DefenseTech Cluster (an autonomous ecosystem of defense technologies), the Green Recovery Cluster (decentralized energy and green reconstruction), and the Human Capital & MedTech Cluster (digital rehabilitation and human capital preservation), along with their comprehensive characterization within Ukraine’s mission-oriented innovation policy framework. The expediency of introducing a social audit of missions to ensure transparency and sustained social consensus is substantiated.

title: Safe and adaptive control of non-stationary stochastic systems via Lyapunov-constrained distributional reinforcement learning
summary: Abstract Non-stationary environments pose significant challenges for reinforcement learning (RL), particularly in safety-critical applications like robotics and energy systems, where adaptability, stability, and robustness to uncertainty ar
content: Abstract Non-stationary environments pose significant challenges for reinforcement learning (RL), particularly in safety-critical applications like robotics and energy systems, where adaptability, stability, and robustness to uncertainty are essential. This paper introduces Lyapunov-Guided Distributional Reinforcement Learning with Entropy Regularization (LG-DRL-ER), a novel framework designed to address these challenges in non-stationary Markov Decision Processes (MDPs). LG-DRL-ER integrates three key components: distributional RL to model the full return distribution, capturing reward uncertainty; Lyapunov stability constraints to ensure safe convergence to a target state; and entropy regularization to promote adaptive exploration. We present a rigorous stability analysis, supported by lemmas and theorems, demonstrating convergence in probability under dynamic conditions. We further establish finite-time convergence guarantees with explicit bounds on the convergence time. An adaptive parameter update rule ensures robustness to changing dynamics, validated through theoretical guarantees and empirical evaluations. Simulations in chaotic and hyperchaotic systems showcase LG-DRL-ER’s superior performance in achieving stable, adaptive control compared to existing methods. This framework advances safe RL by bridging data-driven learning with control-theoretic guarantees, offering significant implications for autonomous systems and dynamic environments.

title: One-Step-Ahead Solar Radiation Forecasting Using Bi-LSTM and GRU Models in Semi-Desert Climates
summary: The increasing demand for energy and the imperative to reduce greenhouse gas emissions have heightened the need for renewable energy sources. Hence, there has been a notable surge in research efforts focused on advancing solar energy foreca
content: The increasing demand for energy and the imperative to reduce greenhouse gas emissions have heightened the need for renewable energy sources. Hence, there has been a notable surge in research efforts focused on advancing solar energy forecasting. The aim of this study is to forecast solar radiation using Deep Neural Network models, including Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), based on historical solar radiation values recorded at half-hour intervals in a semi-desert climate over a two-year period starting in January 2020. To assess and compare the accuracy of the two Deep Neural Networks (DNNs), various evaluation metrics were used, including Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Maximum Error, and R-squared (R²). Solar radiation predictions were carried out based on the values recorded over the previous twenty-four hours at half-hour intervals. The results obtained indicate that both forecasting models achieve exceptional accuracy in one-step-ahead solar radiation prediction, with correlation coefficients exceeding 97.2%. This highlights the strong potential of Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) models for optimizing and estimating solar radiation. Consequently, these models can be effectively used to estimate solar energy production, thereby enhancing the control and efficiency of solar energy systems. However, the study also highlights challenges in forecasting under partial cloud cover, where sudden fluctuations in solar radiation adversely affect prediction accuracy. Addressing these complexities could further improve the robustness of forecasting models and enhance their practical applicability in semi-desert climates.

title: Modelling Industrial Sector Performance on Economic Development in Nigeria
source: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ECONOMICS AND BUSINESS MANAGEMENT
summary: This study examined the effect of industrial sector performance on economic development in Nigeria, with emphasis on the manufacturing, crude oil and natural gas, construction, and electricity subsectors, while real GDP per capita served as
content: This study examined the effect of industrial sector performance on economic development in Nigeria, with emphasis on the manufacturing, crude oil and natural gas, construction, and electricity subsectors, while real GDP per capita served as the proxy for economic development. Annual time series data covering the period 1981–2024 were sourced from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), National Bureau of Statistics (NBS), World Development Indicators (WDI), U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA), and the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC). The study employed the Augmented Dickey–Fuller (ADF) unit root test, the Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) bounds cointegration approach, and the ARDL estimation technique. The unit root test revealed a mixed order of integration of the series, while the Bounds cointegration test confirmed the existence of a long-run relationship among the variables. The ARDL estimates revealed that manufacturing output and electricity generation exert positive and statistically significant effects on real GDP per capita in both the short and long run. Crude oil and natural gas output had a positive and statistically significant effect only in the short run. Construction output exerted a positive but insignificant effect in the short run and a significant negative effect in the long run. The study concludes that industrial sector performance is a critical driver of economic development in Nigeria. It recommends expanding electricity infrastructure through increased public-private partnerships and renewable energy integration, while improving efficiency in the construction sector through effective project monitoring and implementation.

title: Controlling rigid-wing airborne wind energy systems during circular flight without exact path following
summary: Abstract. We propose a feedback architecture that enables effective flight control of rigid-wing airborne wind energy systems during circular-pattern reel out. The controller performs well with only proportional-integral regulators, thereby
content: Abstract. We propose a feedback architecture that enables effective flight control of rigid-wing airborne wind energy systems during circular-pattern reel out. The controller performs well with only proportional-integral regulators, thereby presenting a significantly simpler solution compared to the existing literature. The key idea is in tracking the roll angle on a non-static reference frame, effectively reducing the control problem to one degree of freedom. This method of navigation does not require users to define an exact path for the kite to follow, which contributes to stability and robustness. In its minimum viable form, the controller can function with only ailerons while requiring no pitot-tube measurement, although the addition of elevators and rudder enables angle-of-attack and zero-sideslip tracking for more efficient power generation. Simulation-based verification is conducted on an industrial six-degree-of-freedom model with a flexible tether, nonlinear aerodynamics, and realistic wind conditions, showing satisfactory performance. Three expansions to the control law are then presented. The first one reduces angle of attack fluctuation during reel out by adding a proportional pitch angle feedback term to the elevator, resulting in more power. In the second expansion, the reel-out radius is automatically adjusted to enable phase synchronisation of multiple kites in a farm configuration, where minimum separation rules may apply. The third expansion implements a proportional feedback rule that enables figure-of-eight flight. By using proportional-integral architecture, the controller is easy to implement, making it a suitable baseline system for benchmarking more advanced control laws.

title: Dataset for study 'Multi-season evaluation of temperature and wind in the marine boundary layer along the United States northeast coast in the High-Resolution Rapid Refresh model'

summary: The Third Wind Forecast Improvement Project (WFIP3) was conducted along the US northeast coast from 2024-2025 collecting comprehensive observations in the marine boundary layer. Ground-based remote sensing observations of temperature and wi
content: The Third Wind Forecast Improvement Project (WFIP3) was conducted along the US northeast coast from 2024-2025 collecting comprehensive observations in the marine boundary layer. Ground-based remote sensing observations of temperature and wind were used to evaluate the marine boundary layer in the operational High-Resolution Rapid Refresh (HRRR) model that is run by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. This repository contains the observational and model data as well as the code used to process and analyze the data and to create the plots. A manuscript with the results of this study was submitted to the journal Geoscientific Model Development by Adler et al. 2026 and is available at https://egusphere.copernicus.org/preprints/2026/egusphere-2026-97/ under DOI https://doi.org/10.5194/egusphere-2026-97.
