title: RNN(p) for power consumption forecasting
summary: Abstract An elementary Recurrent Neural Network that operates on p time lags, called an RNN( p ), is the natural generalisation of a linear autoregressive model ARX( p ). It is a powerful forecasting tool for variables displaying inherent s
content: Abstract An elementary Recurrent Neural Network that operates on p time lags, called an RNN( p ), is the natural generalisation of a linear autoregressive model ARX( p ). It is a powerful forecasting tool for variables displaying inherent seasonal patterns across multiple time scales, as is often observed in energy, economic, and financial time series. The architecture of RNN( p ) models, characterised by structured feedbacks across time lags, enables the design of efficient training strategies. We conduct a comparative study of learning algorithms for these models, providing a rigorous analysis of their computational complexity and training performance. We present two applications of RNN( p ) models in power consumption forecasting, a key domain within the energy sector where accurate forecasts inform both operational and financial decisions. Experimental results show that RNN( p ) models achieve excellent forecasting accuracy while maintaining a high degree of interpretability. These features make them well-suited for decision-making in energy markets and other fintech applications where reliable predictions play a significant economic role.

title: Introducing pySRTS: The next generation of the Sub-Regional Timber Supply Model
summary: The Sub-Regional Timber Supply (SRTS) model has been a staple in the analysis and research of the Southeastern U.S. timber market for over two decades. In this paper, we take the existing model and modernize it through a ground-up rewrite a
content: The Sub-Regional Timber Supply (SRTS) model has been a staple in the analysis and research of the Southeastern U.S. timber market for over two decades. In this paper, we take the existing model and modernize it through a ground-up rewrite and reimagining. The updated model includes adding new functionality, such as basin-level price premiums when solving the market equilibrium, and dynamic product weights in the harvest goal program. We document model assumptions, input data, and mathematical formulations in addition to identifying opportunities for users to modify and extend the model. By focusing on flexibility and modularity during the initial development, the pySRTS model is more adaptable to a wide range of research applications. We present a set of illustrative demand scenarios in which a new sawmill opens in North Carolina, U.S. In these scenarios, we explore how the new local prices and model parameterization interact to produce projections of future removals, prices, and forest inventories.

title: Video gaming and health-related components of fitness
source: Open Access at Essex (University of Essex)
summary: Video gaming (VG) is a highly sedentary activity that has increased substantially in popularity over the past decade. Sedentary behaviour is associated with several health issues, including weight gain, cardiovascular and all-cause mortalit
content: Video gaming (VG) is a highly sedentary activity that has increased substantially in popularity over the past decade. Sedentary behaviour is associated with several health issues, including weight gain, cardiovascular and all-cause mortality, and type 2 diabetes mellitus. Therefore, evaluating the physiological and cognitive health-related components of fitness (HRCoF) in VG players (VGP) is important. The primary aim of this thesis was to investigate the relationship between VG and physiological and cognitive HRCoF. Chapter 2 comprised a systematic literature review that synthesised current evidence on the implications of VG for HRCoF in e-athletes and habitual VGP. Six articles were examined, identifying substantial research gaps, including adult male-dominated samples and limited HRCoF assessment. VG participation was associated with faster reaction times. Chapter 3 comprised a cross-sectional observational study investigating relationships between VG duration and HRCoF in adolescents and predicting HRCoF from weekly VG time. Participants were 180 adolescents (12.89 ± 1.43 years). Weekly VG duration and physical activity (PA) were self-reported, while flexibility, balance, handgrip strength, jump height, coordination and reaction time were measured. Generalised additive modelling assessed relationships between VG duration and HRCoF. VG was associated with faster reaction times but negatively associated with flexibility, balance, handgrip strength, jump height and coordination. Relationships with balance, jump height and coordination changed at 32.86, 28.04 and 41.31 h/week, respectively. Sex and age were positive predictors across the six HRCoF. Overall, findings support existing evidence that VG may enhance reaction time, while demonstrating that extended VG duration is negatively associated with other HRCoF in adolescents. This is the first study to identify these relationships in adolescents. Findings may inform parents, educators and policymakers when encouraging a balance between VG and PA. Future research should prioritise longitudinal and intervention studies to establish causality.

title: Invisible consumers: how data deficiencies in energy efficiency of micro- enterprises influence policy design
summary: Micro-enterprises represent major share of EU firms and account for almost 19.8% of EU value added, yet they remain invisible in energy statistics and energy efficiency policy evaluation. This invisibility is not only a matter of missing da
content: Micro-enterprises represent major share of EU firms and account for almost 19.8% of EU value added, yet they remain invisible in energy statistics and energy efficiency policy evaluation. This invisibility is not only a matter of missing data but also a classification problem, since energy use is commonly allocated to household, commercial, or industrial sectors based on metering and contract arrangements rather than enterprise characteristics. As a result, micro-enterprise energy consumption is embedded in sectoral aggregates and cannot be consistently observed as a distinct analytical category. This paper examines how this statistical invisibility might affect the observability of micro-enterprises in energy efficiency policy design and evaluation. It combines a cross-country assessment of data availability across ten EU Member States with a Croatian case study based on a structured survey of 470 micro-enterprises. The survey investigates household-business overlap in workspace use, energy bills, and vehicle ownership. The cross-country review shows that core indicators needed for policy evaluation, including energy consumption, workspace or building use, transport activity, and size specific sectoral classification, are largely unavailable or only observable at aggregated levels. Financial information is available in some countries but remains weakly harmonised. Complementary sources can improve firm level coverage for economic variables but do not resolve the absence of micro-enterprise specific energy consumption data. The Croatian case study provides empirical evidence of extensive household and business overlap. 43% percent of respondents reported on shared household and business energy bills, and 64% report on shared vehicle use. These overlaps indicate that household energy statistics may overstate residential demand while business statistics may underestimate enterprises’ energy needs, with the strongest overlap among the smallest firms. The findings highlight the need to improve the statistical visibility of micro-enterprises and to explicitly account for mixed household and business energy use in both policy design and evaluation. This is particularly relevant for instruments targeting distributional impacts and vulnerability, including measures linked to the Social Climate Fund.

title: Investigating values of forests in Australia through the Nature Futures Framework
summary: Abstract Incorporating diverse values of nature into decision-making is essential for achieving sustainability, particularly in contested policy arenas. Decision-making about forests is highly contested in Australia due to historical legaci
content: Abstract Incorporating diverse values of nature into decision-making is essential for achieving sustainability, particularly in contested policy arenas. Decision-making about forests is highly contested in Australia due to historical legacies, ongoing discourses and emerging challenges. We investigate values that participants from diverse stakeholder groups nationally have of forests in Australia through semi-structured interviews, guided by the Nature Futures Framework (NFF). Results reveal a plurality of values for forests in Australia—the three values most commonly identified were biodiversity and wildlife habitat, cultural and spiritual connections, and wood production, representing one of each of the three NFF value perspectives—respectively, Forests for Nature (FN), Forests as Culture (FC), and Forests for Society (FS). Overlapping values, embodying more than one value perspective, were also evident. First Nations Australians participants expressed predominantly the relational FC value perspective, while others expressed primarily the instrumental FS and intrinsic FN value perspectives. Contestations about the value of wood production remain apparent, but our results challenge the binary narratives that are commonly used to characterise ‘forestry’ and ‘conservation’ interests. Our study demonstrates the potential of using the NFF to guide the exploration of values held by individuals of forests and advances the use of the NFF to facilitate decision-making about forest policy and management. The insights from this paper enhance understanding of the values of forests in Australia and reveal commonalities and differences that can inform more inclusive decision processes about Australian forests. Our results suggest that it is important that these processes incorporate diverse stakeholder voices and embrace a multiplicity of values, including recognising non-Western ways of valuing nature, to facilitate transformative change for sustainability.

title: Sustainable route for the production of starch submicrocrystals: Effect of α-amylase combined with ohmic heating on A-, B-, and C-type starches
summary: This study investigates a sustainable route for the production of submicron starch through a combined approach of ohmic heating (OH) treatment and enzymatic hydrolysis with α-amylase. The effects of electric field frequency (50 Hz, 10 kHz,
content: This study investigates a sustainable route for the production of submicron starch through a combined approach of ohmic heating (OH) treatment and enzymatic hydrolysis with α-amylase. The effects of electric field frequency (50 Hz, 10 kHz, and 20 kHz) during OH pretreatment were evaluated in type A (corn), type B (cassava), and type C (carioca bean) starches. The results demonstrated that OH pretreatment effectively disrupted the granular structure, increased enzymatic accessibility, and promoted the selective degradation of amorphous regions. The synergistic effect of OH and α-amylase hydrolysis was starch-type dependent: for B-type, B50 + E increased crystallinity from 53.2% to 57.1% ( p < 0.05); for A-type, AN+E (48.1%) and A20k + E (50.1%) both increased crystallinity versus native (AN: 40.4%) ( p < 0.05); for C-type, C10k (48.7%) increased crystallinity versus native (CN: 43.7%) ( p < 0.05), while C10k + E (44.6%) did not differ from native ( p > 0.05). This combined approach reduced particle size to the submicron range (≈485–662 nm) and significantly modulated functional properties, including digestibility, gelatinization behavior, and thermal stability. The optimal OH frequency was starch-type dependent: enzymatic hydrolysis alone or 20 kHz for type A, 50 Hz for type B, and 10 kHz for type C. This sustainable and efficient dual-modification strategy represents a promising alternative to conventional acid hydrolysis for production of submicron starch, enabling the design of starch-based materials with tailored structural and functional properties and reduced environmental impact.

title: Assessment tools for the environmental performance of concrete – European classification systems and a novel approach
summary: Abstract In addition to the technological properties of concrete, ecological requirements will become increasingly important in the production of concrete in the future. In recent years, numerous international assessment and classification
content: Abstract In addition to the technological properties of concrete, ecological requirements will become increasingly important in the production of concrete in the future. In recent years, numerous international assessment and classification systems have been developed to transparently communicate and classify the environmental impact of concrete using quantitative parameters. These systems define corresponding classes or levels based on the specific CO 2 -emissions of concrete. Such systems for measuring and classifying CO 2 -emissions of concrete are becoming increasingly important in the planning, tendering, and execution of future construction projects. It is therefore crucial to provide generally applicable methods and classification systems for the assessment of CO 2 -emissions of concrete. This study compares nine recently developed classification systems for evaluating CO 2 -reduced concrete, describing their specific features, limitations and potential. On this basis, a novel approach was developed that combines the international systems into a single concept for compressive strength classes from C20/25 to C50/60. The proposed approach provides a simple and transparent framework that combines existing European classification systems and can therefore support the future implementation of uniform standardized international CO 2 -classes for concrete. In addition, the current practical availability of such CO 2 -reduced concretes is described in relation to the reduction classes of the individual systems.

title: Digital Monitoring, ESG Disclosure and Agricultural Carbon Sink Assetization Efficiency
source: International Journal of Agricultural and Environmental Information Systems
summary: Digital monitoring and ESG disclosure are important for agricultural carbon sink measurement and market-oriented transactions. However, data fragmentation, information opacity, and low conversion efficiency still limit carbon sink assetizat
content: Digital monitoring and ESG disclosure are important for agricultural carbon sink measurement and market-oriented transactions. However, data fragmentation, information opacity, and low conversion efficiency still limit carbon sink assetization. This paper analyzes the coupling mechanism of digital monitoring, ESG disclosure, and agricultural carbon sink assetization efficiency. Based on data from typical agricultural regions, this study builds an indicator system and uses modeling and visualization methods to verify a multi-loop closed-loop mechanism with anomaly handling. Results show that high-quality monitoring and ESG disclosure significantly improve conversion efficiency, while inconsistent policy and lagged market response remain constraints. This study provides a practical framework for agricultural environmental information system integration and supports low-carbon agricultural transformation and carbon finance development.

title: PYRIDINIUM P-TOLUENESULFONATE IONIC LIQUID: SYNTHESIS, CHARACTERIZATION, AND APPLICATION AS CATALYST IN ETHANOL-BASED TRANSESTERIFICATION OF BABASSU OIL
summary: This paper describes the synthesis of the ionic liquid (IL) pyridinium p-toluenesulfonate [HPy][p-TSA], and its characterization as a catalyst in biodiesel production via ethanol-based transesterification of babassu oil. The IL was characte
content: This paper describes the synthesis of the ionic liquid (IL) pyridinium p-toluenesulfonate [HPy][p-TSA], and its characterization as a catalyst in biodiesel production via ethanol-based transesterification of babassu oil. The IL was characterized by FT-IR, ¹H NMR, TG-DSC, and Single-crystal XRD. [HPy][p-TSA] showed an orthorhombic molecular structure and presented 76% w/w yield, and thermal stability up to 300 °C. Factorial design and response surface method (RSM) were applied to optimize and verify the efficiency of [HPy][p-TSA] in ethyl biodiesel production from babassu oil. The Analysis of variance (ANOVA) results showed that at a 95% confidence level, molar ratio EtOH: oil and temperature were the only factors significantly affecting ethyl esters' formation. The best reaction conditions for the process were found at molar ratio alcohol: oil 30:1, IL 1.0% w/w, temperature 200 °C, and reaction time of 8 hours. The maximum conversion rate of biodiesel with pyridinium p-toluenesulfonate was around 79%.

title: Pollution amplifies global water scarcity and hinders progress towards Sustainable Development Goal 6
summary: Water scarcity is commonly assessed as a mismatch between water demand and physical supply, yet this framing can substantially underestimate scarcity when water quality is poor. This critical narrative review synthesizes evidence on how nut
content: Water scarcity is commonly assessed as a mismatch between water demand and physical supply, yet this framing can substantially underestimate scarcity when water quality is poor. This critical narrative review synthesizes evidence on how nutrients, pathogens, heavy metals, persistent organic pollutants, salinity, microplastics, pharmaceuticals, and other emerging contaminants reduce the volume of water that is safe and economically usable. It connects contaminant sources and environmental transformation with treatment burden, ecosystem degradation, climate extremes, socioeconomic impacts, and progress toward Sustainable Development Goal 6 (Clean Water and Sanitation). Anthropogenic pollution impacts almost a third of the world's water supplies and nearly 80% of wastewater is discharged without treatment. Recent global modelling indicates that 55% of the population is exposed to clean-water scarcity for at least one month each year, compared with 47% when only water quantity is considered. Projected exposure may rise to 56–66% by the end of the century under uncertain climate and socioeconomic pathways. Evidence from multiple regions also shows that droughts and heatwaves commonly concentrate pollutants and lower oxygen availability, whereas floods can mobilize contaminants and overwhelm sanitation systems. The review therefore proposes a quality-adjusted scarcity framework, critically compares source control, advanced oxidation, membranes, adsorption, nature-based systems, water reuse, and digital monitoring, and identifies limits to current evidence, including inconsistent mixture-risk assessment, limited full-scale data for emerging technologies, and unequal monitoring capacity. The synthesis indicates that pollution prevention, fit-for-purpose treatment, circular water use, ecosystem restoration, and accountable governance must be pursued together. Increasing supply alone cannot secure water where quality constraints remain unresolved.

title: IMPACT OF DYNAMIC PRICING WITH SMART METERS ON ENERGY CONSUMPTION AND GRID LOAD STABILITY IN ELECTRIC VEHICLE USAGE
source: JAREE (Journal on Advanced Research in Electrical Engineering)
summary: The rapid adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) in Indonesia presents both opportunities and challenges for the national electricity grid. This study analyzes the impact of dynamic electricity pricing, enabled by smart meter technology, on en
content: The rapid adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) in Indonesia presents both opportunities and challenges for the national electricity grid. This study analyzes the impact of dynamic electricity pricing, enabled by smart meter technology, on energy consumption patterns and grid load stability among EV users. Using a quantitative descriptive approach, data were collected from 100 EV users charging their vehicles at smart meter-equipped stations. The study examined variations in electricity consumption and costs across peak, off-peak, and super off-peak periods and analyzed changes in grid load before and after dynamic pricing implementation. Results show that while electricity consumption volumes remain statistically similar across different charging times, the total electricity cost varies significantly due to dynamic tariff differences. EV users who shifted charging to lower-tariff off-peak hours benefited from reduced costs, demonstrating economic incentives to adapt consumption behavior. Furthermore, dynamic pricing contributed to a 10% reduction in peak electricity load and a more even distribution of grid demand during nighttime hours, enhancing grid stability and operational efficiency. In conclusion, dynamic pricing combined with smart metering is an effective approach to managing the growing electricity demands from EV adoption, improving cost efficiency for consumers and promoting a more resilient and sustainable.

title: Population shrinkage in China’s three major urban agglomerations: spatiotemporal patterns and driving factors
summary: Introduction Urban population shrinkage has become a critical challenge confronting sustainable urban development across China. However, systematic cross-regional and multi-type comparative investigations remain scarce in the existing liter
content: Introduction Urban population shrinkage has become a critical challenge confronting sustainable urban development across China. However, systematic cross-regional and multi-type comparative investigations remain scarce in the existing literature. Methods Taking the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei (BTH) region, the Yangtze River Delta (YRD), and the mainland cities of the Guangdong–Hong Kong–Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) as research objects, this paper investigates the spatiotemporal patterns and driving factors of population shrinkage using panel data from 2010 to 2024. A two-way fixed-effects panel regression model is constructed to examine the impacts of multidimensional factors and their regional heterogeneity. Results The findings reveal pronounced regional heterogeneity. The BTH region presents a shrinkage trajectory spreading from peripheral cities to core metropolitan centers; the YRD experiences extensive mild population shrinkage alongside localized severe contraction; whereas the mainland cities of the GBA maintain steady population growth throughout the study period, with no shrinking cities identified. Two-way fixed-effects models further confirm that natural population growth, economic development, and transportation infrastructure constitute the primary drivers, with their impacts exhibiting significant heterogeneity across the three urban agglomerations. Discussion In response to differentiated urban governance needs, this study proposes context-specific smart shrinkage strategies tailored to each urban agglomeration. The findings enrich the empirical literature on urban shrinkage in Chinese megaregions and provide scientific references for sustainable urban management and coordinated regional development policymaking.

title: Combating multidrug-resistant pathogens, breast cancer (MCF-7) and hepatocellular carcinoma (HepG2) using biofabricated zinc oxide nanoparticles
summary: The escalating global burden of multidrug-resistant (MDR) infections and cancer necessitates the development of sustainable and multifunctional therapeutic strategies. Green-synthesized zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnONPs) have emerged as prom
content: The escalating global burden of multidrug-resistant (MDR) infections and cancer necessitates the development of sustainable and multifunctional therapeutic strategies. Green-synthesized zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnONPs) have emerged as promising nanomaterials owing to their unique physicochemical properties, broad-spectrum bioactivity, and environmentally friendly production routes. In this study, ZnONPs were biosynthesized using Citrus sinensis (orange) peel waste extract as a renewable reducing and stabilizing agent. The biosynthesized nanoparticles were comprehensively characterized by UV-Vis spectroscopy, FTIR, XRD, DLS, zeta potential analysis, SEM, TEM, HR-TEM, and SAED. Their antimicrobial, Time-kill kinetics, antibiofilm, antioxidant, and anticancer activities were systematically evaluated against clinically relevant MDR pathogens and human cancer cell lines. The biosynthesized ZnONPs exhibited an absorption peak at 368 nm, a mean hydrodynamic size of 32.45 nm, low polydispersity (0.186), and a zeta potential of - 36.4 mV, confirming excellent colloidal stability and highly crystalline hexagonal wurtzite nanostructures. ZnONPs demonstrated broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity, with MIC and MBC/MFC values ranging from 120 to 512 and 240 to 1024 µg/mL, respectively. Time-kill assays revealed concentration- and time-dependent antimicrobial effects, achieving complete microbial eradication at 4MIC within 8-12 h, while C. albicans remained the least susceptible species. Moreover, ZnONPs significantly inhibited microbial biofilm formation, with inhibition rates ranging from 55.2 to 68.3% at sub-MIC concentrations. Strong antioxidant activity was observed, with DPPH and ABTS radical-scavenging IC₅₀ values of approximately 38-40 μg/mL. Importantly, ZnONPs exhibited potent, dose-dependent, and selective anticancer activity against MCF-7 and HepG2 cells, with IC₅₀ values of 58.98 and 87.93 µg/mL, respectively, while showing minimal toxicity toward normal MCF-10A cells (IC₅₀ > 250 µg/mL; selectivity index > 4.24 for MCF-7 and > 2.84 for HepG2). Confocal microscopy demonstrated preferential and concentration-dependent nanoparticle uptake by cancer cells, which closely correlated with their enhanced cytotoxicity. Mechanistic studies further confirmed apoptosis induction through activation of the intrinsic mitochondrial pathway, as evidenced by significant upregulation of the pro-apoptotic gene BAX (3.4-fold in MCF-7 and 2.9-fold in MDA-MB-231 cells) and marked downregulation of the anti-apoptotic gene BCL2 (0.4-fold and 0.3-fold, respectively; p < 0.0001). Orange peel-mediated ZnONPs exhibit potent antimicrobial, antibiofilm, antioxidant, and selective anticancer activities, underscoring their potential as sustainable multifunctional nanotherapeutics for combating antimicrobial resistance and cancer.

title: From Two Birds to Two Loops: Electric Cooking and the Reinvention of Energy Systems
summary: This paper examines how the body of research and innovation on electric cooking for low and middle income countries has evolved to the extent that electric cooking is now influencing energy system performance. Methods: The paper synthesises
content: This paper examines how the body of research and innovation on electric cooking for low and middle income countries has evolved to the extent that electric cooking is now influencing energy system performance. Methods: The paper synthesises recent evidence from pilots, market developments, and system-level analysis across Africa and Asia, focusing on demand patterns, utility economics, carbon finance mechanisms, and emerging digital and financing models. Results: Electric cooking is increasingly acting as a system-strengthening demand, rather than a system stressor. Two reinforcing mechanisms are identified: (i) an electricity revenue loop, in which increased consumption improves utility and mini-grid viability and supports further investment; and (ii) a carbon finance loop, enabled by metered methodologies and measurable emissions reductions, which can improve household affordability and accelerate adoption. The analysis also highlights the importance of diversified demand (household, commercial, and institutional), which improves load factors and aligns demand with generation. However, a persistent planning blind spot remains, with cooking demand largely excluded from energy models. Conclusions: Electric cooking is moving from proof of concept toward system integration, but scale is constrained by affordability, reliability, tariff design, fuel stacking, institutional fragmentation, and carbon market uncertainty. The findings suggest that electric cooking should be treated as a core component of energy system design, requiring coordinated policy, planning, and financing to realise its full potential.

title: Unmasking Corporate Greenwashing and Its Consequences for Financial System Integrity in Nigeria
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF ECONOMICS AND FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT
summary: This study investigates unmasking corporate greenwashing and its consequences for financial system integrity in Nigeria, with emphasis on firm financial performance, investor behaviour, and corporate governance mechanisms. Using a qualitati
content: This study investigates unmasking corporate greenwashing and its consequences for financial system integrity in Nigeria, with emphasis on firm financial performance, investor behaviour, and corporate governance mechanisms. Using a qualitative and case-based analytical approach supported by secondary data, the study examines how misleading environmental disclosures influence market outcomes and stakeholder trust. Empirical insights reveal that greenwashing significantly reduces firm financial value, particularly Return on Equity (ROE), as firms with higher levels of deceptive sustainability reporting experience weakened investor confidence, increased market volatility, and declining share performance. The findings further indicate that investors are becoming increasingly sensitive to sustainability claims and tend to react negatively to perceived corporate deception, leading to shifts in portfolio allocation and reduced capital inflows. The study also establishes that corporate governance plays a critical moderating role in reducing greenwashing practices. Firms with larger, more independent boards demonstrate lower tendencies toward environmental misrepresentation, highlighting the importance of strong governance structures in promoting transparency and accountability. Various forms of greenwashing are identified, including selective disclosure, decoupling, deceptive labelling, and manipulative reporting. The analysis of high-profile cases such as the Volkswagen Dieselgate scandal underscores the severe financial, reputational, and regulatory consequences of greenwashing. The study contributes to sustainable finance literature by emphasising the need for stronger ESG regulatory frameworks, third-party verification, and enhanced disclosure standards. It recommends stricter enforcement by regulatory bodies, improved investor due diligence, and the establishment of independent sustainability oversight mechanisms within corporate boards. The study concludes that greenwashing undermines financial system integrity by distorting market signals, eroding investor trust, and weakening sustainable finance development in Nigeria, thereby necessitating coordinated policy, governance, and stakeholder responses.

title: The impact of Big Data and AI on innovation management processes
source: Journal of Entrepreneurship and Sustainability Issues
summary: In the era of digital transformation, innovation is becoming a key driver of enterprise competitiveness.This article analyses the impact of digitalisation on the management of innovation processes, focusing on the use of Big Data, artificia
content: In the era of digital transformation, innovation is becoming a key driver of enterprise competitiveness.This article analyses the impact of digitalisation on the management of innovation processes, focusing on the use of Big Data, artificial intelligence (AI), and advanced analytics as critical enablers of strategic decision-making.It examines how these technologies allow organisations to identify innovation opportunities more effectively, optimise product development and respond flexibly to rapidly changing market conditions.The article further discusses the main challenges associated with implementing digital solutions in the innovation process, including data quality issues, technical barriers, and organisational change.Finally, it offers practical recommendations for managers to support sustainable, agile, and data-driven innovation management.

title: Urban green spaces as nature-based solutions for carbon storage and human thermal comfort: evidence from Jimma City, Ethiopia
summary: Urban green spaces provide critical ecosystem services, including carbon storage and thermal regulation, yet their condition remains poorly quantified in many rapidly urbanizing African cities. This study assessed the potential of urban gre
content: Urban green spaces provide critical ecosystem services, including carbon storage and thermal regulation, yet their condition remains poorly quantified in many rapidly urbanizing African cities. This study assessed the potential of urban green spaces as nature-based solutions for carbon sequestration and human thermal comfort in Jimma City, Ethiopia, using a locally calibrated Urban Green Space Condition Index (UGSCI) derived from Landsat 8 imagery and geospatial techniques. Key findings reveal that only 18% of the study area exhibits good green space conditions, with total aboveground carbon stock estimated at 2.18 million Mg C and a mean carbon density of 208.7 Mg C/ha. Dense vegetation stored substantially more carbon per unit area than built-up areas. A strong negative relationship between UGSCI and thermal discomfort (R 2 = 0.61) confirms that improving green space condition significantly enhances urban cooling. The UGSCI framework offers a replicable, low-cost methodology for monitoring urban environmental quality, readily transferable to other rapidly urbanizing cities in the Global South. By establishing a carbon stock baseline for Jimma City and identifying priority areas for green space investment and highlighting environmental justice implications, this study provides evidence-based guidance for sustainable urban planning and climate adaptation, directly supporting progress toward Sustainable Development Goals 11 (Sustainable Cities) and 13 (Climate Action).

title: ROLE OF ETHICAL BRANDING ON CONSUMER BRAND RELATIONSHIPS AND BRAND LOYALTY
source: EPRA International Journal of Research & Development (IJRD)
summary: Corporate ethical branding as a key consumer-related driver in a global market has become a central player in consumer-brand relationship rather than an isolated corporate social responsibility (CSR) approach. This paper is an empirical res
content: Corporate ethical branding as a key consumer-related driver in a global market has become a central player in consumer-brand relationship rather than an isolated corporate social responsibility (CSR) approach. This paper is an empirical research which investigates the effects of ethical branding on trust, brand attachment and long-term brand loyalty. Primary data was collected on a sample of three hundred and fifty diverse consumers using a descriptive research design and a questionnaire of five point Likert scale. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, Multiple Regression and Chi-square tests were employed to examine the brand practices and moderations of various demographic factors. It was found that there is a significant positive relation between ethical consciousness and brand reputation. The multiple regression analysis indicated that the combination of honesty, social responsibility and fair treatment accounts for percent of the re-purchase intentions.. In addition, the Chi-square test showed that income is a key moderator of the consumer's willingness to remain loyal to an ethical brand in a situation where the less expensive alternatives are available. The study concludes that the ethical branding is a strategic tool that builds emotional and brand loyalty as long as the brand is transparent and honest in its operations.

title: Delegating for the Greater Green? How competence and autonomy shape acceptance of agentic AI for carbon-intensive choices
summary: Would you be willing to delegate control to AI for environmental benefits? This study examines users’ willingness to entrust decisions to agentic AI systems designed to promote sustainable behaviours, focusing on how satisfaction of the bas
content: Would you be willing to delegate control to AI for environmental benefits? This study examines users’ willingness to entrust decisions to agentic AI systems designed to promote sustainable behaviours, focusing on how satisfaction of the basic psychological needs – autonomy, competence, and relatedness – mediates intentions to delegate. A 3 × 2 online experiment (N = 1,522) asked participants to evaluate three activities: two carbon-related (food shopping and digital usage) and one non-carbon task (email management), under either full-autonomy or human-in-the-loop conditions. Acceptance differed by context: delegation intentions were lowest for food shopping and highest for digital usage. A preference for human-in-the-loop over fully autonomous systems emerged only in the food domain. Psychological needs fully mediated the advantage of digital usage over email management, but only partially mediated both the food domain's lower intentions and its sensitivity to agency level, suggesting that identity-relevance and hedonic value exert an independent influence beyond the SDT framework. Competence was the strongest mediator throughout, indicating that users favour agentic AI primarily when it credibly enhances their capacity to achieve task goals. Effective sustainable AI design should therefore prioritise utilitarian domains, avoid full automation in identity-relevant contexts, and support competence and autonomy together, preserving user agency.

title: Stakeholder evaluation of livestock scenarios in Switzerland using value-based multi-criteria analysis
summary: CONTEXT,Agri-food systems are multi-functional, leading to unavoidable trade-offs when attempting to transform them for greater sustainability. Addressing these trade-offs while considering food security and balancing social, environmental,
content: CONTEXT,Agri-food systems are multi-functional, leading to unavoidable trade-offs when attempting to transform them for greater sustainability. Addressing these trade-offs while considering food security and balancing social, environmental, and economic welfare could unlock opportunities for meaningful transformation.,OBJECTIVE,This study aims to reveal the unavoidable trade-offs in Swiss livestock production and understand how different stakeholders in the system wish to address these trade-offs.,METHODS,We applied value-focused Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) to assess four contrasting scenarios for the future of Swiss livestock production. These scenarios are business as usual, efficiency, sufficiency, and consistency. We based the relative assessment on (1) the system predictions on 14 key objectives that the sector should fulfill and (2) stakeholder preferences on how to prioritize these objectives. To understand stakeholder preferences, we collected weighting data from 20 representatives across three political clusters: green, conservative, and liberal.,RESULTS AND CONCLUSIONS,Our findings indicate strong disagreement among stakeholders regarding the importance of animal welfare and domestic food production. However, despite these differences, the sufficiency and consistency scenarios were found to be more satisfactory for all stakeholders compared to the business as usual and efficiency scenarios. These results highlight potential pathways for more widely accepted policy interventions.,SIGNIFICANCE,By illustrating key trade-offs and stakeholder preferences, this study provides valuable insights for policymaking in Swiss livestock production and beyond. The findings can help guide the development of more sustainable and broadly supported agricultural policies, e.g. prioritizing goals for reorienting subsidies.

title: How risk and regulation shape the market response to persistent earnings: evidence from Indonesia
summary: This study examines whether systematic risk and the regulatory environment moderate the relationship between earnings persistence and the Earnings Response Coefficient (ERC). Using an 11-year panel of 2,915 firm-year observations from 265 c
content: This study examines whether systematic risk and the regulatory environment moderate the relationship between earnings persistence and the Earnings Response Coefficient (ERC). Using an 11-year panel of 2,915 firm-year observations from 265 companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX, 2011–2021), we estimate fixed-effects panel regressions with firm and year effects, using three profitability-based proxies for earnings persistence (ROE, ROA, OPM) and heteroscedasticity-robust standard errors. Results show that persistent earnings positively and significantly affect ERC, and that this effect strengthens when firms face higher systematic risk and operate under more demanding regulatory conditions. The positive moderating role of systematic risk is attributed to the pro-cyclical return dynamics associated with high-beta stocks, while the regulatory environment amplifies ERC by improving the visibility and verifiability of persistent earnings signals. The study contributes to the earnings quality and capital market literature by providing joint, firm-level evidence that risk and institutional conditions interact to shape investor responses to earnings announcements in an emerging market, a moderating combination that has received limited empirical attention outside developed markets.

title: Understanding Greenwashing Practices in Sustainability Reporting: A Systematic Literature Review
summary: Purpose: This study systematically maps the literature on greenwashing in sustainability reporting by identifying its theoretical foundations, antecedents, mechanisms, consequences, and research gaps.Method: A systematic literature review w
content: Purpose: This study systematically maps the literature on greenwashing in sustainability reporting by identifying its theoretical foundations, antecedents, mechanisms, consequences, and research gaps.Method: A systematic literature review was conducted on 136 Scopus-indexed articles published between 2016 and 2025. Content analysis was used to identify dominant theories, research themes, antecedent factors, mechanisms, and consequences of greenwashing in sustainability reporting.Result: Legitimacy theory, stakeholder theory, and agency theory emerge as the dominant theoretical foundations. Corporate governance, sustainability reporting practices, and firm characteristics are identified as key antecedents of greenwashing, with both direct and indirect effects operating through risk-related mechanisms, including financial and sustainability risks. These relationships are further shaped by external pressures, such as stakeholder pressure, regulatory pressure, and market competition, which may strengthen or weaken firms’ propensity to engage in greenwashing.Practical Implications for Economic Growth and Development: The findings offer insights for companies to improve the credibility of sustainability reporting, investors to make informed decisions, and regulators to strengthen disclosure oversight. These efforts may reduce information asymmetry, improve market transparency, and support efficient capital allocation and sustainable economic growth.Originality/Value: This study provides an integrated mapping of greenwashing in sustainability reporting, covering theoretical foundations, antecedents, risk-related mechanisms, external pressures, consequences, and future research directions.

title: Evolving Perspectives on Clothing and Textiles in Home Economics
source: International Journal of Scientific Research in Science and Technology
summary: This article examines the conceptual evolution of clothing and textiles within Home Economics, now recognized as Family and Consumer Sciences (FCS). Historically framed around early 20th-century domestic skills, garment construction, and fr
content: This article examines the conceptual evolution of clothing and textiles within Home Economics, now recognized as Family and Consumer Sciences (FCS). Historically framed around early 20th-century domestic skills, garment construction, and frugal household management, textile education has transformed into a multifaceted, interdisciplinary research discipline. Driven by mid-century industrialization, post-war consumer behavior, and the formal institutional rebranding codified at the 1993 Scottsdale Conference, modern FCS leverages a human ecology framework to address critical global challenges. Grounded in this paradigm, contemporary textile pedagogy intersects material science, circular economy models, digital technologies, and socio-cultural identity frameworks. The field challenges persistent public misconceptions that reduce textile education to mere manual needlework. Instead, modern FCS curricula incorporate STEAM concepts-including fiber chemistry and 3D digital design-alongside fast fashion critiques, textile recycling, adaptive apparel, and supply chain transparency. Furthermore, emerging research directions embrace artificial intelligence, bio-fabricated textiles, and policy-driven circular economy directives, establishing FCS as a vital platform for environmental stewardship, consumer empowerment, and technological adaptation.

title: Green Corrosion Inhibition and Adsorption Mechanism of Ricinus communis L.Extracts on Mild Steel
summary: Plant-based corrosion inhibitors offer effective corrosion protection, are eco-friendly and safe, biodegradable, low-cost, readily available, and renewable resources, thereby reducing dependence on chemical-based alternatives. Investigating
content: Plant-based corrosion inhibitors offer effective corrosion protection, are eco-friendly and safe, biodegradable, low-cost, readily available, and renewable resources, thereby reducing dependence on chemical-based alternatives. Investigating Ricinus communis L. aqueous extracts as corrosion inhibitors for mild steel in an acidic medium is a significant step toward greater efficiency in corrosion research. The corrosion-inhibition behavior of the extracts was studied using the gravimetric method and electrochemical methods. UV-visible spectroscopy, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, and gas chromatography–mass spectrometry were used to analyze the extract. Field-emission scanning electron microscopy, atomic force microscopy, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy were used to investigate the surface morphology and the protective film. The results suggest that the extracts contain O–H, C–N, and C=C functional groups. These groups play a key role in their corrosion-inhibiting behavior. In an acidic medium, inhibition efficiency increased with increasing extract concentration and decreased with increasing temperature. The inhibition efficiency was maximum at 3 hours, increased with increasing inhibitor concentration, and decreased with increasing temperature. The adsorption isotherm follows Langmuir adsorption, and the thermodynamic parameters indicate that the adsorption follows a mixed-type isotherm. Field emission scanning electron microscopy and atomic force microscopy reveal the adsorption of the extract molecules, showing a smooth surface on the inhibited mild steel. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy supports the formation of C 1s, O 1s, and N 1s of the extract bonding with Fe 2p on the mild steel in the inhibited sample.

title: Greenhouse Renewable Energy Heating, Cooling and Dehumidification: A Case Study for Lesotho
summary: The viability of an energy-sustainable greenhouse in Lesotho and notable, solar photovoltaic thermal (PVT) assisted greenhouse heating, cooling and dehumidification in weather conditions in Lesotho is established. Results for solar PVT assi
content: The viability of an energy-sustainable greenhouse in Lesotho and notable, solar photovoltaic thermal (PVT) assisted greenhouse heating, cooling and dehumidification in weather conditions in Lesotho is established. Results for solar PVT assisted temperature regulation incorporating thermal load assessment, dehumidification modelling, and whole system simulation are presented for two representative locations analysed: Leribe in the lowlands, noted for being the agricultural site in Lesotho, and Mokhotlong in the highlands, typified by cooler weather and prolonged heating needs. The proposed solar PVT-assisted approach supported solar fractions of 87.6% in Leribe and 80.6% in Mokhotlong; energy savings of 6,764–6,936 kWh/year and CO₂ reductions of 1,740–1,944 kg/year; Net Present Values above US$ 53,000, Savings-to-Investment Ratios exceeding 3.0, and a discounted payback period of five years. The study results are encouraging and the next step is to set up a trial on a significant scale to further confirm the merits of solar PVT-assisted greenhouse microclimate control.

title: Beyond the “supply chain” framing: Cattle ranching as a vanishing mediator of deforestation and dispossession in the Brazilian and Colombian Amazon
summary: Unsustainable land-use change has become an increasingly critical social and environmental issue. Over a few decades, vast expanses of land with native vegetation or devoted to mixed-farming systems have given way to large-scale agriculture
content: Unsustainable land-use change has become an increasingly critical social and environmental issue. Over a few decades, vast expanses of land with native vegetation or devoted to mixed-farming systems have given way to large-scale agriculture, incurring considerable biodiversity and livelihood loss. Cattle ranching and the production of a handful of internationally traded commodities such as soy and palm oil play a pivotal role in that expansion. They have led to numerous sustainability initiatives to curb their negative social and environmental impacts, yet a “supply chain” framing poses important limitations, for it typically fails to consider relationships between sectors and broader landscape dynamics. For one, there may be much stronger drivers than food consumption at play. This article draws from the frontier literature and explores the concept of “vanishing mediator” to analyze the role played by cattle ranching in particular. Comparing the Brazilian and Colombian Amazon, we assess how ranching intermediates an ongoing transition between pre-frontier forest areas and capital-intensive monocultures. We draw from land-use data and the scientific literature on each of the two cases as well as on a total of 30 key-informant interviews done in Brazil and Colombia. Our results show that cattle ranching’s role in spearheading deforestation in both countries cannot be understood without reference to its broader context, for it works as a vanishing mediator between pre-frontier settings and industrial agriculture. Ranching occupies frontiers with little infrastructure, paving the way for monocultures; it is instrumental to the land grabbing that makes the endeavor highly profitable; and, crucially, it precariously absorbs and co-opts displaced smallholders. Cattle ranching introduces the latter — as well as incoming settlers — to state institutions that previously neglected them and to a market-driven approach to land use that still preserves the trappings of rural living. Ultimately, however, people migrate to sprawling cities and clear the way for capital-intensive crops such as soy in Brazil and oil palm in Colombia. We conclude that the notion of individualized “supply chains” is shortsighted for dealing with such broader dynamics. Instead, effective sustainability interventions require addressing local vulnerabilities and investing in economic alternatives that can successfully hedge against deforestation drivers.

title: Crop recommendation in precision agriculture: a systematic literature review of methods, trends, and challenges
summary: Crop recommendation methods have become an essential component of modern agriculture, helping farmers identify the most suitable crops based on soil, climatic, and environmental conditions. As key applications of precision agriculture, thes
content: Crop recommendation methods have become an essential component of modern agriculture, helping farmers identify the most suitable crops based on soil, climatic, and environmental conditions. As key applications of precision agriculture, these methods increasingly employ artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL), to improve crop prediction, recommendations, productivity, and farming decision-making. This study presents a systematic literature review (SLR) of ML and DL techniques applied to crop recommendation and related agricultural applications. From 183 identified studies, 129 articles published between 2020 and 2026 were carefully selected through a structured screening process for comprehensive analysis. Relevant studies were retrieved from major academic literature databases and publishing platforms, including ScienceDirect, Scopus, SpringerLink, MDPI, Nature, Frontiers, IEEE, Wiley, and Google Scholar. The review used the PRISMA protocol and showed that ensemble learning-based approaches, particularly Random Forest and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost), are powerful for predictive performance on various agricultural datasets. Traditional ML approaches such as Support Vector Machines, Decision Trees, and k-Nearest Neighbors are still commonly used. At the same time, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks are used for remote sensing and time-dependent agricultural analysis. The most frequently used dataset source is Kaggle, and typical inputs include soil nutrients (NPK), soil pH, weather conditions, and satellite indices such as NDVI and EVI. Many studies have achieved high accuracy, but most are based on static datasets, which reduces their reliability in real-world scenarios. The main research gaps are limited real-time deployment, low integration of multiple data sources, low cross-regional validation, and low model interpretability. The review shows the importance of scalable and explainable AI systems for real applications in agriculture.

title: From Bytes to Businesses: The Role of Digital Technologies in Fostering Sustainable Entrepreneurship in Asia
source: Journal of Asia Entrepreneurship and Sustainability
summary: Digital tools are changing how entrepreneurs across Asia start, scale, and sustain their ventures. Drawing together recent work on digital transformation, financial technology (fintech), and sustainable entrepreneurship, this conceptual pap
content: Digital tools are changing how entrepreneurs across Asia start, scale, and sustain their ventures. Drawing together recent work on digital transformation, financial technology (fintech), and sustainable entrepreneurship, this conceptual paper asks how information technology (IT) adoption helps small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and start-ups pursue economic, environmental, and social goals at once. Building on studies of entrepreneurial orientation, organizational resilience, and green finance, it proposes an integrated framework — tested through eight hypotheses (H1–H8) — in which digital adoption operates as a mediated, moderated pathway to sustainable performance rather than a direct cause of it. The review indicates that IT adoption expands market reach, financial inclusion, and resource efficiency, yet its sustainability payoff hinges on entrepreneurial competencies, infrastructure maturity, and policy support that differ sharply across the region. The paper closes with a proposed empirical design, literature-grounded expectations for each hypothesis, and implications for researchers, entrepreneurs, and policymakers.

title: Angola after the civil war: quantifying the peace dividend using the synthetic control method
summary: This study estimates the impact of peace on economic outcomes in Angola after the civil war ended in 2002. Using the synthetic control method and panel data covering the period 1976-2020, Angola is compared to a data-driven counterfactual w
content: This study estimates the impact of peace on economic outcomes in Angola after the civil war ended in 2002. Using the synthetic control method and panel data covering the period 1976-2020, Angola is compared to a data-driven counterfactual which mimics the country’s socioeconomic characteristics during the pretreatment period. The analysis examines sectors such as agriculture, manufacturing, and services as well as macroeconomic indicators such as foreign direct investment, exports, employment, and consumption as potential channels through which peace may have affected economic performance. Results indicate a large and persistent peace dividend: post-war GDP per capita diverges markedly from the synthetic benchmark and is estimated to be over 40 percent higher on average during 2002-2020 than under the counterfactual. Robustness checks, including placebo tests, leave-one-out exercises, and alternative donor pools, suggest that the findings are not driven by chance or model specification. Overall, the findings highlight the high economic costs of conflict and suggest that the transition to peace was associated with sustained improvements in economic performance, while recognising that these gains occurred within a broader post-2002 macroeconomic environment, including favourable oil market conditions. These results provide important guidance for policymakers seeking long-term stability and growth in post-conflict economies.

title: Effect of hydrocooling on postharvest quality, aroma and biochemical attributes of ‘conference’ pears and ‘sweet dream’ peaches
source: Journal of Food Science and Technology
summary: Abstract This study evaluated the effects of hydrocooling on ‘Conference’ pears and ‘Sweet Dream’ peaches during cold storage (5 and 7 m for pears under regular and controlled atmosphere, respectively, and 15 and 30 d for peaches under regu
content: Abstract This study evaluated the effects of hydrocooling on ‘Conference’ pears and ‘Sweet Dream’ peaches during cold storage (5 and 7 m for pears under regular and controlled atmosphere, respectively, and 15 and 30 d for peaches under regular air) and subsequent shelf-life. Physicochemical, biochemical, physiological, volatile, and sensory parameters were assessed. Overall, hydrocooling slowed ripening, preserved sensory and nutritional quality, and contributed to reducing food waste. Harvest maturity strongly influenced postharvest performance, with fruit firmness and the Index of Absorbance Difference (I AD ) identified as key indicators. Among the treatments, a 10 °C reduction in fruit core temperature (H10) was the most effective, particularly during long-term storage, maintaining firmness, total soluble solids, and titratable acidity. Hydrocooling significantly reduced postharvest disorders (black spot and superficial scald in pears, internal browning and flesh bleeding in peaches) and delayed respiratory peaks, despite similar ethylene and CO 2 patterns across treatments. It also enhanced retention of antioxidant capacity and phenolic compounds, particularly in pears stored under long-term controlled atmosphere (CA). Sensory evaluations showed that H10 enhanced texture-related attributes without negatively compromising flavour. Volatile compound analysis indicated better preservation of key aroma-related esters and aldehydes. Hydrocooling contributed to maintain postharvest quality and extend shelf-life in both species, with H10 often showing the most favourable responses under the conditions tested.

title: Overcoming barriers in hospitality accounting education: A fuzzy-analytic hierarchy process method approach
summary: An accounting education is essential for preparing hospitality professionals to manage financial operations, evaluate performance, and make informed strategic decisions in a data-driven industry. In spite of this, many hospitality students
content: An accounting education is essential for preparing hospitality professionals to manage financial operations, evaluate performance, and make informed strategic decisions in a data-driven industry. In spite of this, many hospitality students continue to struggle with accounting-related coursework, which undermines their ability to succeed in managerial positions. The purpose of this study is to examine persistent barriers that hinder the performance of hospitality students in accounting courses, in recognition of how important financial literacy is to their professional development. In order to uncover insights into the specific challenges students face, we used a fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (fuzzy-AHP) that prioritized key obstacles from the perspective of the students. It was identified that language barriers were one of the most significant factors, particularly for non-native speakers, indicating a pressing need for targeted language support interventions. In addition, students reported limited engagement before and after class sessions, indicating the need to enhance interactive and practical exercises in order to reinforce learning. According to the study, psychological stress and the complexity of accounting terminology had a comparatively lower impact on performance, while technological proficiency had no discernible impact on performance. The findings highlight the importance of integrating language assistance, hands-on applications, and structured engagement strategies to ensure that future hospitality graduates acquire the financial competencies essential for effective management and global competition.

title: Obstacles to Sub-Saharan Africa’s clean energy transition: the ‘tyranny of sovereign ratings’
summary: Sub-Saharan Africa’s clean energy transition is constrained by a financial architecture shaped by persistent perceptions of high risk. Sovereign credit ratings (SCRs) play a central role in determining borrowing costs and access to capital,
content: Sub-Saharan Africa’s clean energy transition is constrained by a financial architecture shaped by persistent perceptions of high risk. Sovereign credit ratings (SCRs) play a central role in determining borrowing costs and access to capital, yet in sub-Saharan Africa they appear misaligned with observed default and recovery outcomes, particularly in infrastructure finance, where default rates are low and loan recovery is high. While high borrowing costs also reflect structural economic, institutional, and political challenges, we argue that prevailing credit rating methodologies and regulatory frameworks amplify these constraints by transmitting sovereign risk mechanically to long-term, asset-backed clean energy investments. Drawing on evidence from multilateral development banks and private infrastructure finance, we show how this misalignment contributes to elevated costs of capital, reinforcing procyclical investment dynamics, and slowing clean energy deployment. We situate this argument within broader debates on climate finance and just transitions, highlighting how distorted risk assessments disproportionately affect the deployment of capital-intensive clean energy in low-income contexts. We conclude by outlining policy-relevant reforms – including adjustments to credit rating practices, recognition of infrastructure as a distinct asset class in financial regulation, and the development of credible Africa-based rating institutions – that could help align financing costs more closely with underlying risks and support a more equitable global energy transition.

title: Noise reduction or idiosyncratic information? ESG performance and stock price synchronicity in China
summary: As environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices become increasingly central to corporate strategy, understanding their impact on capital market efficiency becomes crucial for investors and policymakers. This study examines the rela
content: As environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices become increasingly central to corporate strategy, understanding their impact on capital market efficiency becomes crucial for investors and policymakers. This study examines the relationship between ESG performance and stock price synchronicity using data from Chinese A-share listed companies during 2010-2022. Employing two-stage least squares estimation with regional ventilation coefficients as instrumental variables, we find that ESG performance significantly reduces stock price synchronicity—a result more consistent with the idiosyncratic information hypothesis than with the noise reduction hypothesis that has dominated prior Chinese market studies. We further document a reverse channel whereby high synchronicity prompts firms to strengthen their ESG practices, suggesting that OLS-based estimates of the ESG–synchronicity relationship are likely subject to reverse causality bias; our instrumental variable approach addresses this endogeneity and provides a more credible identification of the causal effect. Mechanism analysis reveals that ESG performance operates through two channels: enhancing corporate innovation and attracting institutional investor investment, both of which facilitate the incorporation of firm-specific information into stock prices. Heterogeneity analysis shows that these effects concentrate among firms with higher analyst coverage, lower financial reporting quality, and private ownership—conditions under which ESG disclosure carries greater informational value for price discovery. These findings carry implications for the design of ESG disclosure standards and governance reforms aimed at enhancing capital market efficiency in emerging markets.

title: Green emulsive liquid-liquid microextraction with spontaneous emulsification and demulsification for the analysis of fungicides
summary: Abstract Succinate dehydrogenase inhibitor fungicides (SFs) are emerging fungicides with unique mechanisms but raise concerns due to their persistence in foods. Reliable quantification of trace SF residues requires efficient and green pretr
content: Abstract Succinate dehydrogenase inhibitor fungicides (SFs) are emerging fungicides with unique mechanisms but raise concerns due to their persistence in foods. Reliable quantification of trace SF residues requires efficient and green pretreatment. Here, a green emulsive liquid–liquid microextraction (ELLME) method using cyclopentyl methyl ether and octyl glucoside was developed. The system enables spontaneous emulsification/demulsification without mixing or centrifugation, ensuring rapid mass transfer and phase separation. A semi-automated workflow allows high-throughput preparation. Coupled with high performance liquid chromatography-ultraviolet detector, recoveries were 85.4–102.8% with RSDs of 0.4–4.8%. Mechanistic studies based on density functional theory and molecular dynamics simulations revealed that van der Waals interactions predominantly drive the spontaneous extraction, while emulsion characterization confirmed the spontaneous phase-separation behavior. Multiple greenness assessment tools validated the sustainable nature of the workflow. In general, this ELLME strategy streamlines sample preparation, minimizes solvent and energy consumption, and provides a practical and sustainable platform for monitoring pesticide residues. Recovery experiments for triazole and strobilurin fungicides showed satisfactory extraction performance, suggesting that the proposed strategy can be extended to structurally diverse pesticides. Overall, the method reduces solvent and energy use and shows potential for broader pesticide analysis.

title: Shift or curtail? How much data-center flexibility is worth depends on the host power grid
summary: Data-center growth risks overbuilding power grid infrastructure and stranding capital. Flexible data-center operation can defer infrastructure investments, but its value depends on the flexibility mechanism and the host power grid character
content: Data-center growth risks overbuilding power grid infrastructure and stranding capital. Flexible data-center operation can defer infrastructure investments, but its value depends on the flexibility mechanism and the host power grid characteristics. We classify data-center load as firm, flexible or interruptible, and embed them in capacity expansion applied to market-organized, fossil-heavy PJM and carbon-capped, centrally coordinated Korea. In PJM, the flexibility value is spatial: shifting workloads between zones reduces system cost by 6% in 2028 and 19% in 2038, avoiding 4.4 GW and 8.9 GW of gas and nuclear generation. In Korea, it is temporal: shifting load into midday solar hours makes 0.5 GW of additional solar worth building in 2028 and avoids 1.2 GW of gas and 0.3 GW of batteries in 2038. In both, realistic event-shape limits diminish the value of curtailment. The results show that flexibility procurement and its value are driven by grid characteristics and policy objectives.

title: Recovery of a NdFeB magnet-rich fraction from full-scale industrial treatment of end-of-life electric scooter motors
source: Waste Management & Research The Journal for a Sustainable Circular Economy
summary: Demand for neodymium-iron-boron (NdFeB) magnets is rising due to their use in clean energy technologies, such as wind turbines and electric cars. Their production based on rare earth elements (REE) creates significant geopolitical and suppl
content: Demand for neodymium-iron-boron (NdFeB) magnets is rising due to their use in clean energy technologies, such as wind turbines and electric cars. Their production based on rare earth elements (REE) creates significant geopolitical and supply chain dependencies. Recycling could mitigate this reliance, yet progress is limited by the absence of a dedicated recovery supply chain. Moreover, devices rich in NdFeB magnets - such as electric motors - are typically processed in plants optimized for the recovery of iron, copper, and aluminum, so REE content is often dispersed within ferrous waste streams because of the ferromagnetic nature of magnets. The aim of our study is to apply a thermal demagnetization step to electric motors prior to the traditional recovery operations for separating ferrous and non-ferrous streams, such as shredding and magnetic separation, to separate a magnet-enriched fraction from the rest of the material flows, without disrupting conventional recycling processes. This approach enables the disintegration of motor components while preserving the downstream recovery of base metals, ultimately producing a magnet-enriched fraction within the non-ferrous matrix. A comprehensive material flow analysis was conducted to quantify and visualize these recovery pathways. Results demonstrated that a portion of the magnet mass bypassed the drum separator and was successfully recovered through an additional magnetic screening step, yielding a magnet-enriched fraction with a final concentration of 50.8% w/w. These findings demonstrate the potential for optimizing pretreatment and separation processes to enhance both NdFeB recovery and separation efficiency, supporting the development of more sustainable magnet recycling systems.

title: Digital Armor: How Digital Transformation Enhances the Resilience of Renewable Energy Enterprises
summary: Enhancing the resilience of renewable energy enterprises is crucial for advancing the energy revolution and building a clean, low-carbon, safe, and efficient energy system. Against the background of an accelerating energy transition and ris
content: Enhancing the resilience of renewable energy enterprises is crucial for advancing the energy revolution and building a clean, low-carbon, safe, and efficient energy system. Against the background of an accelerating energy transition and rising external uncertainty, renewable energy enterprises face multiple challenges, including technological iteration, policy adjustments, and market fluctuations. Thus, enhancing enterprise resilience through digital transformation has become a key issue for promoting high-quality development in the energy industry. Using a sample of Chinese A-share listed renewable energy companies covering the period 2014–2024, this study empirically examines the impact of digital transformation on the resilience of these enterprises and the underlying mechanisms. The results show that digital transformation can significantly enhance enterprise resilience, a finding that remains robust after a series of robustness tests. Mechanism analysis indicates that digital transformation enhances resilience mainly by alleviating financing constraints, optimizing resource allocation, and improving innovation quality. Heterogeneity analysis further reveals that the resilience-enhancing effect of digital transformation varies across enterprises of different sizes and life-cycle stages. This paper provides empirical evidence that renewable energy enterprises can rely on digital technologies to strengthen their risk resilience and improve their sustainable development.

title: Silicon and arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi improve water-use efficiency and drought tolerance in sweet corn
summary: Abstract Maize is a crop that plays a fundamental role in global food security, particularly in tropical and subtropical regions. However, drought stress remains one of the major constraints that limit maize production worldwide. Maize sens
content: Abstract Maize is a crop that plays a fundamental role in global food security, particularly in tropical and subtropical regions. However, drought stress remains one of the major constraints that limit maize production worldwide. Maize sensitivity to water deficit is especially critical during the flowering stage, often resulting in substantial yield losses. This study aimed to investigate a sustainable strategy to mitigate drought stress in sweet corn through the combined application of silicon (Si) and inoculation with arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) in non-sterilized native soil. We hypothesized that the association between Si and AMF could enhance drought tolerance by improving the physiological and agronomic performance of the plants. Our results demonstrated that the combined treatment increased mycorrhizal colonization by 50%, root volume by 53%, soil Si availability, and leaf concentrations of Si and P by 45% and 50%, respectively. Furthermore, under water-deficit conditions, the combined application promoted significant improvements in gas exchange parameters, including increases of 51% in photosynthetic rate, 29% in transpiration rate, 29% in stomatal conductance, and 33% in intercellular CO₂ concentration, as well as a 30% increase in leaf xylem water potential. In addition, water-use efficiency increased by 29%, while industrial yield and soluble solids content increased by 29% and 30%, respectively. These findings provide strong evidence for the synergistic effects of AMF and Si in enhancing drought resilience in sweet corn, highlighting a promising strategy for sustainable agricultural production under water-limited conditions. Further studies are required to evaluate the interaction between Si and AMF using different maize hybrids and AMF strains under drought conditions in natural soils.

title: Yerel Kalkınma Çerçevesinde Kentsel Tarım Stratejileri ve Uygulamaları
source: Ankara Hacı Bayram Veli Üniversitesi İktisadi ve İdari Bilimler Fakültesi Dergisi
summary: Kentsel tarım, yerel kalkınma sürecine doğrudan katkı sağlayabilme potansiyeline sahiptir. Bu doğrultuda araştırmanın amacı, yerel kalkınma çerçevesinde kentsel tarım stratejilerinin ve uygulamalarının ortaya konulmasıdır. Araştırmada kents
content: Kentsel tarım, yerel kalkınma sürecine doğrudan katkı sağlayabilme potansiyeline sahiptir. Bu doğrultuda araştırmanın amacı, yerel kalkınma çerçevesinde kentsel tarım stratejilerinin ve uygulamalarının ortaya konulmasıdır. Araştırmada kentsel tarıma bütüncül çözümler üretmek için iyi uygulama örnekleri eklenerek genel bir bakış açısı sunulmaktadır. Çalışmanın yöntemi, literatür taramasına ve betimsel içerik analizine dayalı nitel bir araştırmadır. Analiz sürecinde genel eğilimleri içeren stratejiler ve politikalar belirlenerek, kentsel tarım uygulamalarının yerel kalkınma sürecine katkısı belirlenmiştir. Bu bağlamda, kentsel tarım uygulamalarının kentsel yaşamda giderek daha önemli hale geldiği, kentsel politika ve stratejilere dâhil edilmeye başlandığı, sağlık, çevre, ekonomik, sosyal ve kültürel yönlere kadar birçok alanda yerel kalkınmayı destekleme potansiyeline sahip olduğu sonucuna varılmıştır.

title: A cross-species perspective on migration in the Anthropocene
summary: Migration, whether of trees, animals or humans, is a universal ecological response to environmental change. Yet scientific and policy frameworks treat these processes in isolation, obscuring their shared temporal structure and coupled dynam
content: Migration, whether of trees, animals or humans, is a universal ecological response to environmental change. Yet scientific and policy frameworks treat these processes in isolation, obscuring their shared temporal structure and coupled dynamics. Reframing migration as a temporally layered, cross-species phenomenon enables more coherent climate governance, more equitable policy, and more effective conservation across taxa, sectors, and regions. This reframing must, however, be grounded in legal authority to act.

title: PARS: an urban context framework for residential adaptive reuse
summary: Housing shortages in rapidly growing metropolitan regions have increased interest in adaptive reuse strategies that enable the residential conversion of existing non-residential buildings. However, most adaptive reuse evaluation approaches
content: Housing shortages in rapidly growing metropolitan regions have increased interest in adaptive reuse strategies that enable the residential conversion of existing non-residential buildings. However, most adaptive reuse evaluation approaches primarily focus on building-level characteristics, while the surrounding urban context that supports everyday residential life remains less systematically operationalised. This study develops a computational framework for evaluating the potential adaptive reuse of office buildings and shopping malls by analysing the urban environments surrounding them. The framework is grounded in the spatial logic of the 15-min city, which emphasises access to daily services and amenities within walkable distances as a key condition for supporting residential life. The empirical analysis focuses on 1,454 office, shopping mall, and commercial-use buildings across Istanbul, derived from the 2024 building inventory of the Istanbul Metropolitan Municipality. For each building, four urban context indicators were calculated to represent complementary dimensions of residential suitability: Population–Amenity Balance (PAB), Amenity Diversity, metro-based Connectivity, and Amenity–Rent Alignment (ARA). These indicators are subsequently aggregated into the Potential Adaptive Reuse Score (PARS), a composite urban-context readiness metric for residential adaptive reuse.
